106.x: Murdock – four universal functions; MacIver – essential/non-essential; Ogburn (with Nimkoff) – seven functions, loss of functions; Parsons – two irreducible functions.

106.s:
Assertion (A): According to Ogburn, the affectional function of the family has not passed to outside agencies.
Reason (R): Ogburn identified four universal functions of the family.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
106.x: A is true: in Ogburn's 'loss of functions' thesis all functions except affection pass to outside agencies. R is false: Ogburn listed seven functions; the four universal functions are Murdock's.

106.s: Who among the following argued that people of India lived mostly in small and simple households?
106.x: A.M. Shah (The Household Dimension of the Family in India, 1973) showed from census and historical data that most Indians always lived in small and simple households; the large joint household was confined to some sections.

106.s: Who said that joint family is an extended kinship group in India?
106.x: Irawati Karve defined the joint family as a group living under one roof, eating from one hearth, holding property in common and related as a type of kindred, i.e. an extended kinship group.

106.s: Author of the book 'Marriage and Family in India'?
106.x: Marriage and Family in India (1955) is by K.M. Kapadia, the pioneer of family studies in India.

106.s: A.M. Shah argued for a conceptual distinction between family and
106.x: A.M. Shah (The Household Dimension of the Family in India) insisted on distinguishing the family from the household.

106.s: Milton Singer's research on ___ focused on the resilience of traditional family and values.
106.x: Milton Singer's study of industrial leaders in Madras (When a Great Tradition Modernizes) found the joint family and its values resilient.

106.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a joint family?
106.x: A joint family has co-residence, common property and common worship; private ownership of property is not its characteristic.

106.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a joint family?
o: All members living in one household
Members need not be related to each other
The entire property belongs to the family
106.x: Joint family members live in one household, hold property in common and pool income, and are related by kinship; 'members need not be related' is false.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. I.P. Desai's Mahuva study identified five degrees of jointness.
2. I.P. Desai found 39% of households nuclear and 61% joint.
3. Ramkrishna Mukherjee found joint families over-represented in trade and higher occupations.
4. Leela Dube argued that the family reproduces patriarchy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 reverses Desai's figures: 61% of Mahuva households were nuclear and 39% joint. The other three are correct.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. K.M. Kapadia is regarded as a pioneer of family studies in India.
2. A.M. Shah wrote The Household Dimension of the Family in India in 1983.
3. For Irawati Karve, jointness rests on functional unity and obligations and may involve common property.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 is wrong on the year: A.M. Shah's The Household Dimension of the Family in India appeared in 1973. Kapadia (Marriage and Family in India, 1955) and Karve's view of jointness are correct.

106.s: 'Dayabhaga' is generally practiced in which state?
106.x: The Dayabhaga school (Jimutavahana) prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara school governs the rest of India.

106.s: In which year Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act introduced?
106.x: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act was passed in 1956 with the Hindu Succession and Minority and Guardianship Acts.

106.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
106.x: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship (Amendment) Bill, 2016 (amending sections 6 and 7 to give mothers equal guardianship) was introduced in 2016 as a private member's bill.

106.x: The Family Courts Act was passed in 1984 (on the 59th Law Commission Report) for matrimonial and family disputes.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the schools of Hindu law:
1. The Mitakshara is Vijnaneshwara's commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.
2. Vijnaneshwara lived at the court of the Rashtrakutas.
3. Under the Dayabhaga, a son gets a right to ancestral property by birth.
4. The Dayabhaga school is associated with Jimutavahana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: Vijnaneshwara lived at the Kalyani Chalukya court, and under the Dayabhaga the son's right arises only on the father's death (by birth is Mitakshara). Statements 1 and 4 are correct.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Succession Act:
1. The 2005 amendment made daughters coparceners by birth under Section 6.
2. In Vineeta Sharma (2020), the Supreme Court held that this applies only if the father was alive in 2005.
3. Andhra Pradesh amended its succession law in 1985, 20 years before the central amendment.
4. B.R. Ambedkar was the main advocate of the Hindu Code, of which the Act forms a part.
How many of the above statements are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Vineeta Sharma (2020) held that the right applies whether or not the father was alive in 2005. The 2005 Sec. 6 change, AP's 1985 amendment and Ambedkar's role are correct, so three are correct.

106.s:
Match List I (law) with List II (what it provides):
List I
a. Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956
b. Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956
c. Family Courts Act, 1984
d. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
List II
i. Maintenance of wives, children, indigent parents and divorced wives
ii. Guardianship among Hindus

106.x: HMGA 1956 – guardianship; HAMA 1956 – adoption; Family Courts Act 1984 – after the 59th Law Commission Report; BNSS 2023 – maintenance provisions.

106.s: Who among the following expressed the opinion that family is the ideal instrument in an exploitative society?
106.x: David Cooper (The Death of the Family, 1971) called the family an ideological conditioning device, the ideal instrument of an exploitative society. Engels linked the monogamous family to private property but did not use this phrase (printed key: Engels).

106.s:
Morgan identified five different family forms. They are:

A. Syndyasmian

B. Punaluan

C. A united family

D. Monogamous

E. Patriarchal family
Select the answer from the codes given below and indicate their correct order as mentioned by Morgan.
106.x: L.H. Morgan (Ancient Society, 1877) gave five forms in order: consanguine ('united'), punaluan, syndyasmian, patriarchal, monogamian, i.e. C, B, A, E, D.

106.s: A Nair family is called

106.s: In which of the following tribes does property inherit to the youngest daughter?
106.x: Among the Khasi of Meghalaya the youngest daughter (ka khadduh) inherits the ancestral property.

List I
a. Nair (Kerala)
b. Tiyans, some Moplas and Bants
c. Khasi (Meghalaya)
d. Garo (Meghalaya)

106.x: Nair tharavad – Marumakkathayam, abolished by the Kerala Act of 1975; Tiyans/Moplas/Bants – tharawad of a woman, her siblings and her sisters' children; Khasi – ultimogeniture; Garo – Machong lineage, Nokma heads.

106.s:
Assertion (A): In matrilineal systems, power usually remains with women.
Reason (R): Among the Khasi, the youngest daughter inherits the property.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
106.x: A is false: even in matrilineal systems power usually stays with men, such as maternal uncles (matriliny is not matriarchy). R is true – Khasi ultimogeniture.

106.s: Which of the following is the main factor behind the disintegration of the joint family system in India?
106.x: Industrialisation and urbanisation (migration for jobs, wage work, small urban housing) are the main forces breaking up the joint family; laws, women's education and freedom are secondary factors.

106.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a modern family?
106.x: The modern family shows financial independence of members, decline of religious control and greater freedom for women; increased religious feeling is not its trait.

106.s: What has Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu recently advocated?
o: Replacing joint families with nuclear households
A return to the joint family and incentives for families with two or more children
A two-child limit with penalties for larger families
106.x: In the context of declining fertility, Naidu urged a return to the joint family and incentives for having two or more children.
xa: **NFHS-6** TFR **2.0**; NFHS-5 urban TFR **1.6**.
AP's **1985** succession amendment preceded the central **2005** amendment by **20 years**.

106.s: Which one of the following is a major family-related consequence of urbanisation and migration?
o: Break-up of joint families due to rural-urban migration
Strengthening of joint ownership of agricultural land
106.x: Limited urban housing and rural-urban migration contribute to the break-up of joint families.
106.tq: Link the stated social factor with its specific structural consequence.
xs: **Rural-urban migration** breaks up **joint families** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Limited housing** in cities adds to this.
xa: Census **2001 → 2011**: rural joint households fell **20.1% → 16.8%**; urban **16.5% → 14.6%**.
⚠ **Singer, Orenstein**: industrial urbanisation has **not dissolved** the joint family.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the changing Indian family:
1. Industrialisation turns the family from a production unit into a consumption unit.
2. The Hindu Succession Act, labour laws and rational education are among the factors changing the family.
3. Women's employment has led to fewer female-headed households.
4. Urbanisation eliminates all emotional bonds of joint families.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: women's employment brings more female-headed households, and urbanisation does not eliminate all emotional bonds of joint families. Industrialisation (production to consumption unit) and law and education (Hindu Succession Act, labour laws) are correct factors.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rise of single-parent and female-headed households is due mainly to the expansion of joint-family residence.
2. T.K. Oommen studied urban families by livelihood, authority structure, social milieu and value pattern.
3. For Oommen, the proprietary class has joint families with strong elder-male authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: single-parent and female-headed households rise with widowhood, marital instability and male migration, not joint-family expansion. Oommen's criteria and the proprietary class are correct.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about high-risk families:
1. They face severe social, economic, health, psychological or environmental challenges.
2. A debt burden is a psychological cause of high-risk families.
3. Social exclusion is a social cause of high-risk families.
4. Elderly care in Indian families has traditionally rested on filial piety.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
106.x: Only statement 2 is wrong: debt is an economic cause (with poverty); psychological causes are stress and addiction. The rest are as in the notes.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about households (Census 2001 to 2011):
1. The share of rural nuclear households rose from 50.7% to 52.1%.
2. The share of urban nuclear households rose from 52.3% to 54.3%.
3. The share of rural joint households fell to 16.8%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 reverses the urban trend: urban nuclear households fell from 54.3% to 52.3%. Rural nuclear households rose (50.7 → 52.1%) and rural joint households fell (20.1 → 16.8%).

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NFHS-6 (2023-24) had the International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai as nodal agency.
2. NFHS-6 puts India's total fertility rate at 2.0.
3. NFHS-5 put the urban total fertility rate at 1.6.
4. Average household size fell from 4.6 to 4.2 in NFHS-5.
How many of the above statements are correct?
106.x: Statement 4 is wrong: household size fell from 4.6 to 4.4. IIPS Mumbai (MoHFW), TFR 2.0 in NFHS-6 and urban TFR 1.6 in NFHS-5 are correct, so three are correct.

107.s: Which law first made legislative provision for inter-caste marriage in India?
107.x: The Special (Civil/Native) Marriage Act, 1872 first made legislative provision for civil, including inter-caste, marriage; the Hindu Marriage Act came only in 1955 and the Hindu Code Bill was never enacted as such.

107.s: Which state in India has common civil code?
107.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
107.x: Goa has a common civil code – the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867, extended to Goa in 1870. (Since 27 January 2025 Uttarakhand also enforces a Uniform Civil Code, but it is not among the options.)

107.s: According to the Civil (local) Marriage Act, 1872, what is the marriageable age for the girl and boy?
107.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
107.x: The Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872 fixed the marriageable age at 14 for the girl and 18 for the boy; 21/18 belongs to the Special Marriage Act, 1954.

107.s: On July 30 2019, India banned ____.
107.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
107.x: On 30 July 2019 the Rajya Sabha passed the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Bill, banning instant triple talaq (up to 3 years' jail).

107.s: As per the child Marriage Act 2006, which of the following is not a crime
o: For an adult male to marry a minor child wife
To perform or help for child marriage in any way
To allow, encourage or fail to stop a child marriage (as a parent or guardian)
107.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
107.x: The PCMA 2006 punishes an adult male who marries a child (Sec. 9), anyone who performs or abets a child marriage (Sec. 10) and parents/guardians who promote it or fail to stop it (Sec. 11); merely taking part as a guest is the option the key treats as not a separate crime.

107.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929:

A. It is also known as Sharda Act

B. It was brought to curb the practice of getting girls married before the age of puberty

C. In 1929, it fixed the age at marriage for girls to 15 years

D. The punishment those who violated the act was minimum three years of rigorous imprisonment
Choose the correct statements from the following:
107.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (A and B only); it is added as option 5.
Statements A (known as the Sharda Act) and B (to curb marriage of young girls) are correct. C is wrong – the 1929 Act fixed the girls' age at 14 (boys 18), raised to 15 only in 1949; D is wrong – punishment was simple imprisonment or fine, not three years' RI. No printed option gives 'A and B only' (official key: A, B and C).

107.s: This act was the first legislative provision in India to provide consent for the performance of inter-caste marriages?
107.x: The Special (Civil/Native) Marriage Act, 1872 was the first law to permit civil, including inter-caste, marriage; the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 came much later (same question as Civil Services 'first legislative provision for inter-caste marriage').

107.s: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in the following year?
107.x: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955 – the first codified Hindu marriage law after Independence.

107.s: What is the amount to be paid to the bride at the time of divorce in a Muslim marriage?
107.x: Mehr is the sum fixed at marriage and payable to the bride (prompt or deferred, e.g. on divorce); talaq and khula are forms of divorce and dahej is dowry.

107.s: Marriage is considered as a sacred institution in Indian Culture. There are different religious personal laws that lay down marriage law in India. In which of the following Acts is the registration of marriage compulsory ?
107.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Panchayat Secretary
107.x: Under the Special Marriage Act the marriage is entered in the Marriage Certificate Book, so registration is compulsory; under the Hindu Marriage Act (Sec. 8) registration is optional.

107.s: The main objective of The Sharda Act of 1929 was
o: To ban the dowry given by the bride to the bridegroom
To fix the minimum age of 14 years for marriage of females and 18 for males
107.x: The Sharda (Child Marriage Restraint) Act, 1929 fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 for girls and 18 for boys; it did not deal with dowry, kanyashulkam or education.

107.s: After a landmark Judgement on Triple Talaq in 2017, which among the following methods of Which divorce practised in Muslim society was recently challenged in the Apex Court of India?
107.x: Talaq-e-Hasan, with talaq pronounced once a month over three months, was challenged in the Supreme Court after the 2017 triple talaq verdict. Talaq-e-Ahsan is a single pronouncement plus iddat and is not the one challenged.

107.s: Which is the only State in India to have the Common Civil Code?
107.x:
Goa is no longer the only State – now Uttarakhand also enforces a Uniform Civil Code, in force since 27 January 2025 (newsonair.gov.in).
Goa was the only State with a common civil code – the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867, extended to Goa in 1870 (now Uttarakhand too: its Uniform Civil Code is in force since 27 January 2025).

107.s: What is "Mehr" under Muslim law?
o: An amount fixed at the time of marriage to be paid to the bride in case of divorce
Marriage ceremony expenses paid to religious leader
Fine paid to the community for repudiation of wife
Penalty paid by wife for desertion of husband
107.x: Mehr is the amount fixed at the time of marriage and payable to the bride, falling due at the latest on divorce or the husband's death; it is not a ceremony fee or a penalty.

107.x: Muslim marriage (nikah) is a civil contract – an agreement – not a sacrament as Hindu marriage traditionally is.

107.x: Muta (Mutah) is the temporary contract marriage recognised among (Shia) Muslims.

107.s: By what other name was the Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872 known?
107.x: The Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872 was also called the Native Marriage Act. It provided a monogamous civil marriage, with ages of 14 for the girl and 18 for the boy.

107.s: Up to how many years of imprisonment does the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 provide for instant triple talaq?
107.x: The 2019 Act punishes instant triple talaq with up to 3 years' jail plus fine; seven years is in the Assam polygamy Bill.

107.s: Which legislation was the first Child Marriage Restraint Law in India?
107.x: The Sarda Act (Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929) was the first law restraining child marriage. The Age of Consent Act, 1891, was an earlier measure but not a restraint law.
n: The Sharda Act was the first Child Marriage Restraint Law in 1929. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Child Marriage Restraint Act, also called the Sharda Act, was the first comprehensive child marriage law in 1929. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Age of Consent Act was the first legal measure against child marriage in 1891. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was the first Widow Remarriage Act in 1856. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Special Marriage Act was the first Special Marriage Law in 1872. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: The **Sharda Act** (Child Marriage Restraint Act), **1929**, was the **first Child Marriage Restraint Law** — option **(4)**.
The **Age of Consent Act** (**1891**) was the **first legal measure** against child marriage, but not a restraint law.
The **Special Marriage Act, 1872** was the first special marriage law.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say the Special (Civil) Marriage Act **1872** prohibited child marriage; its ages were **14 (girl) and 18 (boy)**.
**PCMA 2006**: minimum age **18 (women) / 21 (men)**; such a marriage is **voidable**.
NFHS-6: **20.1%** of women aged 20-24 married before 18.
**Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat**: eliminate child marriage **by 2030**.

107.s: Which was the first codified Hindu marriage law after Independence?
107.x: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was the first codified Hindu marriage law after Independence; the 1872 Act was the first special marriage law.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955:
1. It applies to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.
2. It applies to Scheduled Tribes in all cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: The HMA covers Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, but applies to STs only if notified.

107.s: What are the minimum marriageable ages under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?
107.x: PCMA 2006 fixes 18 years for women and 21 for men; a child marriage is voidable at the child's option.

107.s: The Sikh Anand Karaj marriage is solemnised:
107.x: Anand Karaj takes place in a gurdwara; a Nikah is conducted by a Kazi and a Special Marriage Act marriage by a Marriage Officer.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about marriage laws in India:
1. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides for inter-religious civil marriage before a Marriage Officer, with marriageable ages of 21 for men and 18 for women.
2. Divorce under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is provided by Section 13.
3. Divorce by mutual consent was added to the Indian Divorce Act, 1869 in 2001.
4. Registration of marriages was added to the Anand Marriage Act, 1909 in 2012.
How many of the above statements are correct?
107.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: divorce under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is provided by Section 27; Section 13 is the divorce section of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The notes: SMA 1954 – Marriage Officer, ages 21/18, divorce Sec. 27; mutual consent added to the Indian Divorce Act in 2001; Anand Marriage Act registration added 2012.

a. Age of Consent Act, 1891
b. Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Muslim personal law:
1. A Muslim marriage (Nikah) is solemnised by a Kazi, under the Kazis Act, 1880.
2. Talaq-e-Ahsan is a single pronouncement of talaq followed by the iddat period.
3. Khula is a divorce at the husband's instance, without the wife's consent.
4. Talaq-e-Hasan is talaq pronounced once a month over three months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: khula is divorce at the wife's instance, by mutual consent. The rest follow the notes: Nikah is solemnised by a Kazi (Kazis Act 1880); Talaq-e-Ahsan = a single pronouncement + iddat; Talaq-e-Hasan = once a month over three months.

1. Goa's common civil code is based on the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867, brought into Goa in 1870.
2. Uttarakhand's UCC, in force since 27 January 2024, makes the registration of live-in relationships mandatory.

107.x: Levirate is the custom by which a widow marries her deceased husband's brother; marrying the deceased wife's sister is sororate.

o: Marriage with her deceased husband's brother
107.x: Devara Nyayam is the Telugu name for levirate: a widow marries her deceased husband's brother. Marriage with a sister's daughter is menarikam.

o: A woman having only one man as her husband
A woman marrying a man and his brother
107.x: Polygamy means having more than one spouse at a time; of the options only 'a woman marrying many men' (polyandry, a form of polygamy) describes plural marriage. B is monogamy; C (husband and his brother) is also polyandry but only its fraternal sub-type, so A is the better answer.

107.s: If a man marries more than one sister (Several Sisters) it is called this.
107.x: A man marrying several sisters is sororal polygyny; option C ('conjugal polygamy') is the translated rendering of that term. Levirate is marriage with a deceased husband's brother and endogamy is marriage within the group.

107.s: A woman is married to her husband's brother. This marriage is called
107.x: A woman married to her (deceased) husband's brother is levirate, called Devara Nyayam in Telugu; 'justice for wife and sister' is sororate.

107.s: Devara Nyaya is marriage of a man
o: Childless, with his dead brother's wife
107.x: Devara Nyayam (levirate) is a man's marriage with his dead brother's widow; marriage with the late wife's sister is sororate.

107.s: When the wife's husbands are brothers, then it is called as?
107.x:
Most books and keys: fraternal polyandry (A). Strictly: adelphic polyandry (B) is a synonym and equally correct.
When a woman's husbands are brothers it is fraternal polyandry (Toda). 'Adelphic polyandry' is only a synonym of the same thing; sororate and levirate concern a dead spouse's sibling.

107.s: Once a man marries a woman once it is
107.x: One man married to one woman is monogamy; polygamy and polyandry involve more than one spouse.

107.s: What is Levirate?
o: Marriage to wife's sister while wife is alive.
Marriage of wife's sister after death of wife.
Marriage to husband's brother while husband is still alive.
Marriage to husband's brother after death of husband
107.x: Levirate is the marriage of a widow to her deceased husband's brother; marriage to the wife's sister after her death is sororate.

107.s: Which of the following systems correctly reflects the marriage of a widower with his wife's sister?
107.x: A widower marrying his deceased wife's sister is sororate, rendered in Telugu papers as 'Bharya Bhagini Nyayam' (justice for spouses); Devara Nyayam is levirate.

107.s: What is the marriage of a woman with her husband's brother called?
107.x: Marriage of a woman with her (deceased) husband's brother is levirate, Devara Nyayam in Telugu; 'justice for spouses' is sororate.

107.s:
Which is the correct order of succession for the following forms of marriage adopted by the Toda tribal people of the Nilgiri Hills?

A. Monogamy

B. Polygamy

C. Polygamy
Using the codes given below, select the correct answer.
107.x: The stem is garbled (the third item should read polyandry). The Todas moved from fraternal polyandry to polygyny and finally monogamy, so the order is C, B, A (UPSC 1997 key).

107.s: The religion which permitted widow marriage was:
107.x: Islam has always permitted widow remarriage; Hindu widow remarriage was legalised only in 1856. Moved to the marriage row.

107.s: Levirate is practiced in which societies?
107.x: Levirate - a widow marrying her dead husband's brother - keeps the widow, her children and property within the husband's lineage, so it belongs to patriarchal (patrilineal) societies. (Moved to the marriage row of Society.)

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Levirate (Devara Nyayam), in which a widow marries her deceased husband's brother, is practised among the Gond and Munda.
2. Under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 a bigamous marriage is void.
3. Fraternal (adelphic) polyandry, where a woman's husbands are brothers, is found among the Toda and Khasa.
4. Under sororate (Bharya Bhagini Nyayam) a widower marries his deceased wife's sister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: a bigamous Hindu marriage is void under HMA Section 11; Section 12 deals with voidable marriages. Levirate (husband's brother; Gond, Munda), fraternal polyandry (Toda, Khasa) and sororate (wife's sister) are as in the notes.

107.s: Allowing a woman to marry a man of low caste where a man is not allowed to marry a Lower Caste person. This type of practice is called?
107.x: As worded, the stem describes a woman marrying a man of lower caste, which is hypogamy (pratiloma). Hypergamy (anuloma) is the reverse: a woman marrying a man of higher caste.

107.s: What is the name of inter caste marriage if a man of lower caste marries a woman of higher caste?
107.x: A lower-caste man marrying a higher-caste woman is pratiloma (hypogamy) and was condemned; anuloma is a higher-caste man with a lower-caste woman.

107.s: What is a marriage outside a certain relationship group called ?
107.x: Marriage outside a defined group of relations is exogamy; endogamy is marriage within the group, and hypergamy/hypogamy concern caste rank.

107.s: A marriage within the same caste is thus called
107.x: Marriage within one's own caste is endogamy (Telugu antar-vivaham), which the translated paper renders as 'intermarriage'; 'extramarriage' stands for exogamy.

107.s: Recently the Delhi High Court has upheld the constitutional validity of a provision of the Hindu Marriage Act which 'prohibits marriage between people who are related to each other through ancestors from their parent's side unless their customs allow them to do so'. The said provision was mentioned in which Section of the Hindu Marriage Act?
107.x: Section 5(v) of the Hindu Marriage Act bars marriage between sapindas unless custom permits; the Delhi High Court upheld it in 2024. 5(iv) is prohibited degrees, 12 voidable marriages, 13 divorce.

107.s: A marriage ceremony between a high caste girl and a low caste boy is called
107.x: A high-caste girl marrying a low-caste boy is pratiloma marriage (condemned); anuloma is the reverse (high-caste man, low-caste woman).

107.s: Marriage of a high caste girl to a low caste boy is called
107.x: A high-caste girl marrying a low-caste boy is pratiloma (hypogamy); anuloma is a high-caste man with a low-caste woman, and endogamy/exogamy are rules about the group.

107.s: Hypogamy marriage means a marriage between:
o: A man of high caste and a woman of low caste
A man and a woman of high caste
A woman of high caste and a man of low caste
107.x: Hypogamy is a woman of higher caste marrying a man of lower caste (pratiloma); hypergamy (anuloma) is a higher-caste man with a lower-caste woman.

107.s: Why is taboo observed in the society?
o: To avoid sexual contact between certain relatives
To raise the status of women
107.x: A taboo is a social prohibition; the classic one, the incest taboo, forbids sexual contact between certain relatives and so enforces exogamy. Respect for elders, dislike of enemies and women's status are not why taboos exist.

107.s: Menarikam marriage will happen to whom?
o: Children of siblings of the same sex
107.x: Menarikam (Telugu) is marriage with the mother's brother's daughter, a cross-cousin, i.e. children of opposite-sex siblings; parallel cousins (same-sex siblings' children) cannot marry.

107.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Anuloma from Pratiloma marriage?
o: Anuloma involved a lower-varna man and Pratiloma a higher-varna man.
Anuloma was condemned, whereas Pratiloma was generally tolerated.
Anuloma involved a higher-varna man and a lower-varna woman, whereas Pratiloma involved the reverse.
Both terms denoted marriage between members of the same varna.
107.x: Anuloma referred to a higher-varna man marrying a lower-varna woman and was tolerated. Pratiloma referred to a lower-varna man marrying a higher-varna woman and was condemned.
107.tq: Compare the direction of varna status and then apply the approval distinction.
xs: **Anuloma** = a **higher-varna man** marrying a **lower-varna woman**; **Pratiloma** = the reverse — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the definitions, and option (2) reverses the judgement: it was **Pratiloma** that was **condemned**.
Neither term means same-varna marriage; that is **endogamy**.
xa: Anuloma is also called **hypergamy**; Pratiloma is **hypogamy**.
**Endogamy** operates at the **varna, caste, sub-caste** level; **Ghurye** saw it as the defining feature of caste.
⚠ **Levirate** = husband's brother; **Sororate** = wife's sister.

107.s: Which of the following statements about endogamy is incorrect?
107.x: Option C is incorrect: endogamy, marriage within the group, keeps caste boundaries firm rather than weakening them. It also preserves group identity and controls how property passes.
107.tq: Recall what endogamy does to caste boundaries.
n: Endogamy preserves group identity. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 51-52]
Endogamy maintains caste boundaries. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 51-52]
Endogamy controls property transfer. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 51-52]
Endogamy includes marriage within a caste. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 51-52]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is option **(3)**: **endogamy** **maintains** caste boundaries; it does not weaken them.
Endogamy also **preserves group identity** and **controls property transfer**.
xa: Endogamy = marriage **within** one's own caste, tribe or religion.
It **promotes cultural continuity** and **social solidarity**.
**Exogamy** bars marriage within one's **gotra**.
North India: caste endogamy + **gotra exogamy** + **village exogamy**.

107.s: Under Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which of the following is NOT a stated condition for a valid Hindu marriage?
o: The bridegroom and bride have completed 21 and 18 years respectively.
The parties must belong to the same sub-caste.
The parties are not within the prohibited degrees of relationship.
Neither party has a living spouse at the time of marriage.
107.x: Belonging to the same sub-caste is not a condition under Section 5. The section includes conditions relating to a living spouse, age, prohibited degrees and sapinda relationship, subject to custom in the last case.
107.tq: Separate statutory conditions from a social practice not included in the provision.
xs: **Belonging to the same sub-caste** is **not** a condition under **HMA Sec. 5** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Sec. 5(i)**: **no living spouse**; **Sec. 5(iii)**: ages **21/18**; **Sec. 5(iv)**: not within **prohibited degrees** — options (4), (1), (3) are all real conditions.
xa: **Sec. 5(v)**: parties must **not be sapindas** unless custom permits — upheld by the **Delhi HC**.
Sapinda (**Sec. 3(f)**) = **3** generations (mother's side) / **5** (father's side).
A marriage with a living spouse is **void** under **Sec. 11** and punishable as bigamy (**IPC 494** = **BNS 82**).

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. G.S. Ghurye regarded endogamy as the defining feature of caste.
2. The traditional North Indian pattern of mate selection combines caste endogamy, gotra exogamy and village endogamy.
3. Irawati Karve analysed the concepts of sapinda and gotra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: North India combines caste endogamy and gotra exogamy with village EXOGAMY – daughters are married into distant villages. Ghurye (endogamy the defining feature of caste) and Karve (sapinda and gotra) are correct.

107.s:
Assertion (A): Exogamy is the rule of marrying within one's own caste, tribe or religion.
Reason (R): The incest taboo, which forbids sexual contact between certain relatives such as parents and children or siblings, is the basis of exogamy.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
107.x: A is false: marriage within one's own caste, tribe or religion is endogamy; exogamy is marriage outside a group (sapinda, sagotra, village exogamy). R is true: the notes describe the incest taboo as the basis of exogamy.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955:
1. Under Section 3(f), the sapinda relationship extends to five generations on the mother's side and three on the father's.
2. Section 5(v) bars a marriage between sapindas unless custom allows it.
3. In January 2024 the Delhi High Court upheld Section 5(v).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 reverses the numbers: Section 3(f) counts 3 generations on the mother's side and 5 on the father's. Statements 2 (Sec. 5(v) sapinda bar, unless custom allows) and 3 (Delhi HC, Jan 2024, upheld it) are correct.

107.s: Who defined marriage as "a covenant to bear and nurture children"?
107.x: Malinowski defined marriage as a contract for the production and maintenance of children; Westermarck stressed a durable union beyond procreation, and Murdock and Tylor gave no such definition.

107.s: Which of the following was the custom practised during the ancient period that allows married women to cohabit with a designated male for the sole purpose of procreating a child if her husband was impotent or had died?
107.x: Niyoga is the ancient custom in which a wife cohabits with a designated man to bear a child when her husband is impotent or dead; the other options are not names of this custom.

107.s: A consensual and informal relationship practised in accordance to matrilineal laws of Kerala that prevailed among Namboothiris and Nairs is known as:
107.x: Sambandham was the consensual, informal union of Namboothiris and Nairs under Kerala's matrilineal system.

107.s: Marriage by purchase of bride was known as
107.x: Marriage by purchase of the bride, with the groom's family paying a bride price, is the Asura form (option 'Asara' is a misprint). Paisacha is by deceit, Rakshasa by abduction, Prajapatya is an approved form.

107.s: What is the correct order of succession in terms of the main goals of marriage in traditional Hindu society ?
107.x: Hindu marriage has three aims in descending order: Dharma (religious duty) first, then Praja (progeny), and Rati (pleasure) last (K.M. Kapadia).

107.s: 'Marriage is the only rite performed by women, so it is said that marriage is necessary for them'. This statement is given by?
107.x: K.M. Kapadia (Marriage and Family in India) wrote that marriage was the only sacrament (samskara) for a woman, hence obligatory for her.

107.s: Marriage according to traditional Hindu belief is:
107.x: In traditional Hindu belief marriage is a sacrament – a holy, indissoluble bond – not a contract. (Off-topic: moved to the marriage row.)

107.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Brahma Marriage is regarded as the highest form of marriage.
Arsha Marriage involves a symbolic gift such as a cow and a bull from the groom.
Prajapatya Marriage involves the purchase of the bride by giving wealth to her family.
Daiva Marriage involves giving the daughter to a priest who officiates a sacrifice.
107.x: Option C is incorrect: buying the bride with wealth is Asura marriage. Prajapatya marriage stresses duty, family welfare and children.
n: Daiva Marriage involves giving a daughter to a priest performing a sacrifice. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Prajapatya Marriage is based on duty and family life. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Brahma Marriage is considered the highest form of marriage. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Daiva Marriage involves giving the daughter to a Ritvik priest. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
The Ritvik priest in Daiva Marriage officiates a sacrifice. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Daiva Marriage is linked with religious rituals. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
The groom in Daiva Marriage is a priest. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Arsha Marriage is performed after receiving a symbolic gift such as a cow and a bull from the groom. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Prajapatya Marriage emphasizes family welfare. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Prajapatya Marriage emphasizes procreation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Asura Marriage involves the groom giving wealth to the bride's family. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Asura Marriage involves purchasing the bride. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Asura Marriage involves a bride price. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Arsha Marriage involves receiving symbolic gifts from the groom. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Asura Marriage involves purchasing the bride by giving wealth to her family. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Arsha Marriage involves only a symbolic exchange. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
Prajapatya Marriage is performed with blessings emphasizing duty. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-76]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is option **(3)**: purchasing the bride with wealth is **Asura** marriage, not **Prajapatya**.
**Prajapatya** emphasizes **duty**, **family welfare** and **procreation**.
**Brahma** is the highest form; **Arsha** involves a **cow and a bull**; **Daiva** gives the daughter to a **Ritvik priest**.
xa: **Asura** is **disapproved**: a **bride price**, with wealth as the primary consideration.
**Arsha** was common among **sages** and **hermits**.
In Prajapatya, **husband and wife share responsibilities**.

107.s: With which varna is Rakshasa marriage, seen in abduction marriages of the epics, associated?
107.x: Rakshasa marriage is linked with Kshatriyas, and abduction marriages appear in the epics; buying the bride is Asura.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Form of marriage (Manu Smriti))
a. Brahma
b. Daiva
c. Arsha
d. Asura
List-II (Meaning)
i. Daughter given to a priest officiating at a sacrifice
ii. Groom pays a bride price (purchase of the bride)
iii. Daughter given to a learned, virtuous groom, without dowry or bride price
iv. Marriage after symbolic gifts of a cow and a bull from the groom
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Brahma = daughter given to a learned, virtuous groom with no dowry or bride price (the highest approved form); Daiva = daughter given to the officiating priest; Arsha = symbolic gifts (cow and bull) from the groom; Asura = purchase of the bride (disapproved).

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the forms of marriage in the Manu Smriti:
1. Manu Smriti recognises eight forms of marriage, four approved and four disapproved.
2. Gandharva marriage, illustrated by Shakuntala and Dushyanta, is one of the four approved forms.
3. Paisacha marriage, by deceit or intoxication without consent, is the most condemned form.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Gandharva (love, mutual consent – Shakuntala–Dushyanta) is a disapproved form, only conditionally accepted. Eight forms (4 approved, 4 disapproved) and Paisacha as the most condemned are as in the notes.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Later Vedic period Swayamvara became more common and widow remarriage was encouraged.
2. The Satyashodhak marriage, started by Savitribai Phule, was held without dowry and without a Brahmin priest.
3. Niyoga allowed a wife to cohabit with a designated man to beget a child when her husband was impotent or dead.
How many of the above statements are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is wrong: in the Later Vedic period child marriage began, Swayamvara declined and widow remarriage was discouraged. Statements 2 (Satyashodhak marriage – Savitribai Phule; no dowry, no Brahmin priest) and 3 (Niyoga) are correct.

107.s: Divorce occurs when
o: When husband and wife decide to live separately
When both spouses inform their parents
When the society believes that their marriage bond is broken
When the marriage is annulled by the court
107.x: Divorce is the legal dissolution of a marriage by a court (W.P. Scott: an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage); spouses merely deciding to live apart is separation, not divorce.

107.s: Chapter XX of the Indian Penal Code deals with
107.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
107.x: Chapter XX of the IPC (Sections 493–498) dealt with offences relating to marriage (bigamy is Sec. 494); now BNS Sections 81–84.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. W.P. Scott defined divorce as 'an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage relationship and allowing each partner the right to remarry'.

II. The first legislation in respect of the dissolution of marriage in India was enacted in 1869, and is 'Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act'.

III. The irresponsible departure from the home on the part of husband, leaving the family to fend for itself is called as 'the poor man's divorce'.
Which of the above given statements are correct?
107.x: I is W.P. Scott's definition of divorce and III is desertion, 'the poor man's divorce' – both correct. II is wrong: the 1869 law is the Indian Divorce Act (Christians); the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act dates from 1865.

107.s: In May 2023, the Supreme Court said that "it can exercise its powers under Article ___ of the constitution to grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of a marriage" even if one of the parties opposes it.
107.x: In May 2023 (Shilpa Sailesh) the Supreme Court held it can use Article 142(1) to grant divorce on irretrievable breakdown of marriage even if one party opposes.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Section of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955)
a. Section 11
b. Section 12
c. Section 13
d. Section 13B
List-II (Subject)
i. Divorce by mutual consent
ii. Bigamous marriage void
iii. Voidable marriages
iv. Grounds of divorce, including not heard of as alive for 7 years
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Sec. 11 – bigamous marriage void; Sec. 12 – voidable marriages; Sec. 13 – grounds of divorce (adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, unsoundness of mind, renunciation, not heard of for 7 years); Sec. 13B – divorce by mutual consent.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Desertion – the husband leaving the family to fend for itself – is called 'the poor man's divorce'.
2. Under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939 a wife may seek divorce if maintenance has not been paid for 3 years.
3. IPC Chapter XX (Sections 493–498) on offences relating to marriage corresponds to BNS Sections 81–84.
4. The Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill, 2025 makes polygamy cognizable and non-bailable, with up to 7 years' rigorous imprisonment.
How many of the above statements are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 1939 Act ground is non-payment of maintenance for 2 years. Desertion as 'the poor man's divorce', IPC Ch. XX = BNS 81–84 (bigamy IPC 494 = BNS 82) and the Assam Bill 2025 (cognizable, non-bailable, up to 7 years' RI) are as in the notes.

107.s:
Assertion (A): In May 2023 (Shilpa Sailesh) the Supreme Court held that it can dissolve a marriage on irretrievable breakdown under Article 142(1) even if one party opposes.
Reason (R): Irretrievable breakdown of marriage is a ground of divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
107.x: A is true (Art. 142(1), Shilpa Sailesh, May 2023). R is false: irretrievable breakdown is not an HMA ground – the Supreme Court in Naveen Kohli (2006) only urged that it be made one; that is why the Court relies on Art. 142.

107.s: In which case, the Supreme Court held in 2016 that "forcing husband to get separated from his parents, amounts to cruelty"?
107.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
107.x: In Narendra v. K. Meena (2016) the Supreme Court held that a wife forcing her husband to separate from his parents without a justifiable reason amounts to cruelty, a ground for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act.

107.s: People decide that living together with committed intimate, sexual relationships which also provides a way to share daily life is seen
107.x: Two partners who choose to live together in a committed intimate relationship, sharing daily life without marrying, are cohabiting; marriage needs social and legal sanction, and singlehood means living without a partner.

107.s: In which of these months, the Indian Supreme Court overruled a 2014 Madras High Court ruling, stating that advocates can indeed solemnize “self-respect” marriages under the Hindu Marriage Act’s Section 7(A)?
107.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
107.x: In August 2023 the Supreme Court overruled the 2014 Madras HC ruling and held that advocates can solemnise self-respect marriages under Sec. 7-A.

107.s: Which is the first South Asian Nation to formally register same sex marriage?
107.x: Nepal was the first South Asian nation to register a same-sex marriage (2023). India, the Maldives and Bhutan have not done so.

107.s: In which case did the Supreme Court in 2006 urge that irretrievable breakdown be made a ground of divorce?
107.x: In Naveen Kohli (2006), the Supreme Court urged irretrievable breakdown as a ground of divorce.

107.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a contemporary trend in marriage?
107.x: Companionate marriage, rising age at marriage, serial monogamy and increasing divorce are identified trends. Universal return to child marriage is not one of them.
107.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of the stated social trends.
xs: A **universal return to child marriage** is **not** a listed trend — option **(2)**.
**Uberoi** lists **companionate marriage**, **rising age at marriage**, **serial monogamy** and **more divorce** — options (1), (3), (4) are genuine trends.
xa: Child marriage is in decline under policy: **Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat** aims to eliminate it **by 2030**.
**NFHS-6**: still **20.1%** of women aged 20-24 married before 18.
Inter-caste marriage is only **about 5%**.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Case)
a. Narendra v. K. Meena (2016)
b. Shayara Bano (2017)
c. Navtej Singh Johar (2018)
d. Supriyo (2023)
List-II (Ruling)
i. Instant triple talaq unconstitutional
ii. No same-sex marriage under the Special Marriage Act
iii. Forcing the husband to separate from his parents is cruelty
iv. Consensual same-sex relations decriminalised (Section 377)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Narendra v. K. Meena (2016) – forcing the husband to separate from his parents = cruelty; Shayara Bano (2017) – instant triple talaq unconstitutional; Navtej Singh Johar (6 Sep 2018, 5-judge bench) – Sec. 377 read down; Supriyo (Oct 2023) – no same-sex marriage under the SMA.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Self-respect marriages, started by Periyar, were validated by Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act, inserted by a Tamil Nadu amendment in 1967.
2. In August 2023 the Supreme Court held that advocates can solemnise self-respect marriages, overruling a 2014 Madras High Court ruling.
3. In the Supriyo case (October 2023) the Supreme Court read same-sex marriage into the Special Marriage Act, with CJI Chandrachud writing for the majority.
4. In 2010 the Supreme Court protected live-in relationships under Article 19.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Supriyo held there is no same-sex marriage under the SMA, and CJI Chandrachud was in the minority. Statement 4 is wrong: live-in relationships were protected under Article 21. Statements 1 and 2 (Periyar, Sec. 7-A, TN 1967; advocates may solemnise, Aug 2023) are correct.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Patricia Uberoi identified companionate marriage and serial monogamy as contemporary trends.
2. The Dr Ambedkar Scheme gives Rs 5 lakh to inter-caste couples, though inter-caste marriages are only about 5% of all marriages.
3. In July 2026 the Allahabad High Court held that the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act overrides the personal-law 'puberty' rule for all religions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong on the amount: the Dr Ambedkar Scheme gives Rs 2.5 lakh to inter-caste couples (inter-caste marriages are about 5%). Statements 1 (Uberoi) and 3 (Allahabad HC, 1 Jul 2026) are correct.

107.s: Which of the following is not a reason for child marriage
o: Low level of education of girls
107.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
107.x: Poverty, low education of girls and social customs and traditions all drive child marriage; 'status symbol' is not a cause.

107.s: What was the theme of the first 'International Day of the Girl Child' that was observed on 11 October 2012?
o: Empowering Adolescent Girls: Ending the Cycle of Violence
The Power of the Adolescent Girl: Vision for 2030
107.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
107.x: The first International Day of the Girl Child (11 October 2012) had the theme 'Ending Child Marriage'; 'Empowering Adolescent Girls: Ending the Cycle of Violence' was 2014 and 'Girl Force: Unscripted and Unstoppable' was 2019.

107.s:
Match the states in column A with the child marriage data in column B, as per the report of the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) available up to the year 2021 published by Ministry of Women and Child Development in August 2023.
Column A (States):

I. Karnataka

II. Assam

III. Tamil Nadu
Column B (Child marriages registered under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006 in the year 2021):

a. 169

b. 155

c. 273
107.x: NCRB data for 2021 (PCMA cases): Karnataka 273, Assam 155, Tamil Nadu 169 – so I-c, II-b, III-a.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about child marriage in India:
1. NCRB's Crime in India 2023 recorded 6,038 cases under the PCMA, about six times the 2022 figure, with Assam accounting for nearly 90%.
2. According to NFHS-6, 20.1% of women aged 20–24 were married before 18.
3. The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat initiative aims to eliminate child marriage completely by 2026.
4. The PCM (Amendment) Bill, 2025 proposes raising the minimum marriageable age of women to 21.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat aims to cut child marriage by 10% by 2026 and to eliminate it by 2030. NCRB 2023 (6,038 cases; Assam nearly 90%), NFHS-6 (20.1%) and the 2025 Bill (women's age to 21) are as in the notes.

107.s: ' Diku Andi ' means:
o: Marriage by exchange in Koya and Savara tribes
Marriage by capture in Naga tribes
Marriage by probation in Kuki tribe
Marriage by negotiation in Ho tribes
107.x: Diku Andi is the Ho tribe's marriage by negotiation, a later form borrowed from Hindus ('diku' = outsider). Ho marriage by capture is Oportipi.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Way of acquiring a mate)
a. Capture
b. Service
c. Exchange
d. Purchase
List-II (Example)
i. Atta Satta in Rajasthan
ii. Parallels the Asura form
iii. Naga, Ho, Bhil, Gond
iv. Groom works at the bride's home (Gonds)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Capture – Naga, Ho, Bhil, Gond; Service – the groom works at the bride's home (Gonds); Exchange – Atta Satta (bride exchange) in Rajasthan; Purchase (bride price) – parallels the Asura form of Manu.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Ho term)
a. Andi
b. Oportipi
c. Raji-khushi
d. Anader
List-II (Meaning)
i. Marriage by capture
ii. Intrusion – the girl forces herself into the lover's home
iii. Traditional arranged marriage with bride price (gonong)
