122.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: bankruptcy/indebtedness was first (38.7%) and farming-related issues second (19.5%).

122.s: Which state accounted for maximum number of human trafficking cases in 2016?
122.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
122.x: NCRB Crime in India 2016: West Bengal reported the most human-trafficking cases (3,579, about 44% of the national total), ahead of Rajasthan (1,422). Maharashtra and Delhi were far lower.

122.s:
Which of the following is / are included in the Directive Principles of State Policy?

A. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour

B. Prohibition of consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of other drugs which are injurious to health
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
122.x: Only B is a Directive Principle: Article 47 asks the State to prohibit, except for medicinal purposes, intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs. A (prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour) is Article 23, a Fundamental Right (Right against Exploitation), not a DPSP.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about human trafficking:
1. The UNODC regards India only as a high-origin country, not a destination country.
2. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1956 as SITA and renamed in 1986.
3. As per NCRB's Crime in India 2020, there were 696 Anti Human Trafficking Units across States/UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
122.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the UNODC regards India as both a high-origin and a high-destination country.

122.s: The practice of Jogin in Telangana is more prevalent in the district of

122.x: Among the options the Jogini practice is most prevalent in the old Mahbubnagar district (about 2,000 Joginis in Mahbubnagar alone); Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam have it only marginally. (A printed key of Karimnagar is not supported.)

122.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016

122.s: What is that crime, which when tried is punishable, but when done the culprit crime doer cannot be punished?
122.x:
Sec. 309 IPC is gone — now the BNS 2023 (in force 1 July 2024) has no general attempted-suicide offence (Sec. 226 covers only an attempt to coerce a public servant), and MHCA 2017 s.115 presumes severe stress (app notes 2:122 sub 1; general knowledge, not checked)
Suicide: an attempt was punishable under Sec. 309 IPC, but a person who completes it cannot be punished. Murder, theft and rape are punishable whether attempted or committed. (Now: attempted suicide is no longer a general offence – the MHCA 2017 s.115 presumes severe stress, and the BNS 2023 has no Sec. 309 counterpart.)

122.s: Tele-MANAS is a tele-mental-health helpline launched on 10 October 2022. What is its toll-free number?
122.x: Tele-MANAS was launched on 10 October 2022 and can be accessed through the toll-free number 14416.

It is a **tele-mental-health helpline**.
xa: **Sec. 115**, **MHCA 2017** — presumes severe stress; no trial or punishment for attempted suicide.
ADSI 2024: **1,70,746** suicides; **daily wagers** about **31%**.

2. Section 309 IPC punished an attempt to commit suicide with simple imprisonment up to one year and/or fine.
3. The Law Commission in its 210th Report recommended retaining Section 309 IPC.
How many of the above statements are correct?
122.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 210th Report recommended deleting Section 309.

122.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, attempt to suicide remains a general offence.
Reason (R): Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 presumes severe stress in a person who attempts suicide and bars trial and punishment.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
122.x: A is false: the BNS (in force 1 July 2024) has no general attempted-suicide offence; Sec. 226 covers only an attempt to suicide to coerce a public servant. R is true: MHCA 2017 Sec. 115 presumes severe stress and the State must provide care.

122.s: Which State has topped the list of States with the most number of beggars, as per data released by the Union Ministry of Social Justice?
122.x: The Social Justice Ministry's Census 2011 data (4,13,670 beggars and vagrants) put West Bengal first (81,224), then Uttar Pradesh (65,835), Andhra Pradesh (30,218) and Bihar (29,723).

Match List-I (Law / decision) with List-II (Position on begging):
List-I | List-II

d. SMILE (MoSJE, 2022) | iv. Comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
122.x: Bombay Act 1959 – punitive model; Delhi HC 2018 – decriminalised begging; SC 2021 – refused a ban, calling begging a socio-economic problem; SMILE 2022 – rights-based rehabilitation ('Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat').

122.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Uttar Pradesh (65,835) is second after West Bengal (81,224); Andhra Pradesh (30,218) is third.

122.s: The chronic use of drugs and alcohol results in

122.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Social Purity Association (1891) was founded by R. Venkataratnam Naidu.

3. 'Dharya Sparsa – Operation Flush-Out' against drugs and illegal liquor was launched by the Chittoor Police.

122.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the ex gratia under GO 43 is ₹7 lakh.

123.s: Which Constitutional Article gives the States the right to promote educational interests of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes of India?
123.src: Assistant BC, Social, Tribal Welfare Officer Screening Test
123.x: Article 46 (DPSP) directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, in particular SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

123.s: Which of the following practices leads to social exclusion?
123.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
123.x: Separate (segregated) special schools keep blind children apart from mainstream schooling, so they lead to exclusion; inclusive education in ordinary schools is the alternative. Segregation is one of the practices of exclusion.

Which of the following is mainly considered for relation to social exclusion?

A. Caste
B. Gender
C. Race
D. Tribes
Choose the correct answer.
123.x: Social exclusion is studied along caste, gender, race/ethnicity and tribe (and religion, disability, region), so all four (A, B, C, D) apply.

123.s: What is the main objective of providing reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes under the Indian Constitution?
o: To provide them free education abroad
To achieve social justice and equal opportunity
123.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
123.x: Reservations for SCs, STs and OBCs (Arts. 15(4), 16(4), 330, 332) aim at social justice and equality of opportunity for historically excluded groups; the other options are absurd.

123.s: Under which article of the Constitution are the states given right to promote the educational interests of the Scheduled castes and Scheduled tribes and other backward classes of India?
123.x: Article 46 (DPSP) asks the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially SCs and STs.

123.s:
Social exclusion results in the following:

A. Adversely effecting human capital development

B. Bridging historical divisions

C. Widening inequalities

D. Driving social unrest and crime
Select the correct answer:
123.x: Social exclusion hurts human-capital development, widens inequalities and can drive unrest and crime (A, C, D). 'Bridging historical divisions' is the opposite – exclusion deepens them.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT a practice leading to social exclusion?
o: Denied access to land and water
123.x: Untouchability, segregation and denied access to land, water and jobs lead to exclusion; MGNREGA wage employment is a policy response to it.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about social exclusion:
1. Denial of property, work and mobility to women is exclusion based on caste.
2. Social exclusion is a process that is involuntary and systematic.
3. The term was coined by René Lenoir in France in 1974.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: denial of property, work and mobility to women is gender-based exclusion; caste-based exclusion is exemplified by untouchability.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In August 2026 the Union opposed a creamy layer for SCs and STs.
Reason (R): Income alone is enough to end caste-based exclusion.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: A is true (10 Aug 2026). R is false: the Union's ground was the opposite – income alone does not end caste-based exclusion.

Match List-I (Basis of social exclusion) with List-II (Example):
List-I | List-II
a. Caste | i. Adivasis in remote areas
b. Gender | ii. Untouchability against SCs
c. Disability | iii. Segregated special schools
d. Race / tribe | iv. Denial of property, work and mobility

123.x: Caste – untouchability; gender – denial of property, work, mobility; disability – lack of access, segregated special schools; race/tribe – Adivasis in remote areas, racial discrimination.

123.s: Which one of the following is not one of the objectives of the MGNREGA Act?
o: Providing higher education for rural youth
Strengthening the livelihood resource base of the poor

MGNREGA has been replaced — now the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 (in force 1 July 2026, 125 days) (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)

123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev

123.s: Who among the following are eligible to benefit from the ‘Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act’?
o: Adult members of only the scheduled caste and
Adult members of Below Poverty Line (BPL)
Adult members of households of all backward
123.x:
MGNREGA was replaced — now the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 (in force 1 July 2026) guarantees 125 days per rural household (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)
Adult members of any rural household who volunteer for unskilled manual work are eligible; the Act is not limited to SC/ST, BPL or backward-class households. (Now VB-G RAM G, 125 days, from 1 July 2026.)

123.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : MGNREGA is providing employment to at least one member of the eligible household for a minimum period of 100 days in a year.
Reason (R) : Right to employment is enumerated in Part III of the Constitution.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
123.x:
the 100-day guarantee was replaced — now 125 days under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, in force 1 July 2026 (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)
A is true: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage work a year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer. R is false: the right to work is a Directive Principle (Art. 41), not a Fundamental Right in Part III. (Now 125 days under VB-G RAM G from 1 July 2026.)

123.s: Select the one which is not the responsibility of Gram Sabha under the ‘Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005’.
o: The recommend projects to the gram panchayat and prepare list of possible works.
To receive application for work and issue a rated receive.
To monitor the execution of works within the gram panchayat.
To conduct regular social audits of all projects taken up within the gram panchayat.
123.x: The Gram Sabha recommends works, monitors them and conducts social audits. Receiving applications for work and issuing dated receipts is the Gram Panchayat's job, so option 2 is not the Gram Sabha's responsibility.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:

3. NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, starting in Anantapur district.

123.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: NREGA was renamed MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. It guarantees at least 100 days of wage work in a financial year to every rural household.
2. If work is not provided within 15 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is due.
3. At least half of the workers must be women.
4. The Gram Sabha holds social audits, while the Gram Panchayat receives work applications and issues dated receipts.
How many of the above statements are correct?
123.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: at least one-third (not half) of the workers must be women. Note also that the right to work is not a Fundamental Right in Part III; the Act follows Art. 41 (DPSP).

123.s:

Assertion (A): The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026.
Reason (R): The VB-G RAM G Act guarantees 125 days of work per rural household per year.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: Both are true (passed 18 Dec 2025, in force 1 July 2026; 125 days, wage floor ₹300/day), but the 125-day guarantee is a feature of the new Act, not the reason it replaced MGNREGA.

123.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh ranked first (2.10 crore person-days in the first 45 days).

b. NREP

123.x: IRDP (1978-79 pilot, nationwide 2 Oct 1980) → NREP (1980) → JRY (1989, merged NREP and RLEGP) → SGSY (1999). So d, b, c, a.

123.s: At present, with which name is Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (1999) implemented? A) B)
123.x: SGSY was restructured in 2011 as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, branded 'Aajeevika' (renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016). MGNREGA is wage employment, not SGSY's successor.

123.s: The objective of integrated Rural Development Program is to
123.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
123.at: Help families who live below the poverty line to enhance their income, state of living & empowerment
123.x: IRDP (1978-79 / 2 October 1980) aimed to lift rural BPL families above the poverty line through self-employment assets financed by subsidy and bank credit.

123.s:
Match List-I (Programme) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. TRYSEM (1979) | i. Merged PMRY and REGP
b. DWCRA (1982-83) | ii. Sub-scheme of IRDP for rural women
c. JRY (1989) | iii. Merged NREP and RLEGP
d. PMEGP (2008) | iv. Training rural youth for self-employment
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: TRYSEM – training rural youth for self-employment (IRDP component); DWCRA – IRDP sub-scheme so benefits reach rural women; JRY – merged NREP and RLEGP; PMEGP – merged PMRY and REGP (credit-linked subsidy through KVIC).

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The SGSY (1 April 1999) merged IRDP, TRYSEM and DWCRA.
2. The credit-linked subsidy under PMEGP is routed through NABARD.
3. DAY-NRLM ('Aajeevika', 2011) was a restructuring of the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana.
How many of the above statements are correct?
123.x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the PMEGP subsidy is routed through KVIC. 3 is wrong: NRLM restructured SGSY, not JRY.

123.s: The difference between urban and rural average monthly per capita expenditure, in India in 2011-12, was around:
123.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
123.x: NSS 68th round (2011-12, MMRP): average MPCE was about Rs 1,430 rural and Rs 2,630 urban, a gap of about Rs 1,200 (urban about 84% higher).

123.s: The main cause for poverty of rural and tribal people is?
123.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
123.x: The expected key is illiteracy: lack of education keeps rural and tribal people out of better jobs and perpetuates the cycle of poverty. Unemployment is itself largely a result of low education and skills; 'economic status' just restates poverty.

123.s: What is being poor compared with others in the same society called?
123.x: Relative poverty means being poor in comparison with others in the same society; absolute poverty is spending below a fixed poverty line.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's official poverty line is based on income.
2. Size of the house is not one of the social indicators of poverty.
3. The concept of the 'culture of poverty' was propounded by Oscar Lewis in 1959.
How many of the above statements are correct?
123.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the official poverty line is consumption-based (MPCE), not income-based.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Absolute poverty is measured by a fixed poverty line (MPCE cut-off).
2. As per the NSS 68th round (2011-12, MMRP), MPCE was about ₹1,430 in rural and ₹3,630 in urban areas.
3. Multidimensional poverty is measured by the National MPI of NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: urban MPCE was about ₹2,630 (a gap of about ₹1,200 over rural ₹1,430), not ₹3,630.

123.s: Which Indian organization is responsible for estimating the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
123.x: The National MPI is built by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, and NITI Aayog (successor of the Planning Commission) is the nodal agency for poverty estimation. The RBI and the Finance Ministry do not estimate it.

123.s: As per NITI MPI 2023, which State had the lowest multidimensional poverty?
123.x: Kerala recorded the lowest MPI poverty and Bihar (33.76%) the highest.

123.s:
Match List-I (Body / survey) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. NITI Aayog | i. Built with UNDP and OPHI
b. NSO's HCES | ii. Consumption survey about every 5 years
c. PLFS | iii. Nodal agency for poverty estimation
d. National MPI | iv. Standard for unemployment data
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: NITI Aayog – nodal agency for poverty estimation (uses NSSO data); HCES – about every 5 years, its MPCE sets the line; PLFS – standard for unemployment data; National MPI – NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the PLFS:
1. Usual status measures activity over a reference year.
2. Current Weekly Status uses a reference period of 30 days.
3. Current Daily Status records activity for each day of the reference week.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: CWS uses a reference period of 7 days.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Multidimensional Poverty Index:
1. It has three equally weighted dimensions and 12 indicators.
2. Nutrition is an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension.
3. Bank accounts is an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension.
How many of the above statements are correct?
123.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: nutrition is a health indicator; standard of living covers cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, housing, electricity, assets and bank accounts.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's National MPI 2023 (2019-21 data):
1. India's multidimensional poverty headcount was 14.96%.
2. Bihar recorded the highest level (33.76%).
3. Andhra Pradesh (6.06%) was ranked 5th.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh, with 6.06%, was ranked 9th.

123.s: As per National sample Survey Organization the unemployment rate in 2017-18 was a 45 year high at Y) was
123.x: NSO's first PLFS (2017-18) put the unemployment rate at 6.1%, the highest since 1972-73 ('45-year high'), though NSO said the series is not strictly comparable. (Now 3.2% in 2023-24.)

123.s:
Match List-I (Type of unemployment) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Disguised | i. Extra workers add near-zero output
b. Structural | ii. Temporary, while changing or searching for jobs
c. Cyclical | iii. Fall in labour demand in a slowdown
d. Frictional | iv. Mismatch between skills and jobs
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Disguised – more workers than needed (agriculture); structural – skills–jobs mismatch; cyclical – slowdown cuts labour demand; frictional – temporary, while switching or searching.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Disguised unemployment is mainly found in the urban labour market.
2. Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in agriculture.
3. Educated unemployment is predominantly an urban phenomenon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: disguised unemployment is found mainly in agriculture (family farms); frictional and educated unemployment are urban.

123.s:
Consider the following statements (PLFS):
1. India's unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24.
2. Andhra Pradesh's unemployment rate in 2023-24 was 4.1%.
3. Andhra Pradesh's labour force participation rate in 2023-24 was 57.5%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: AP's LFPR (PLFS 2023-24) was 47.5%.

123.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was poverty in 2023-24 as measured by the Tendulkar line?
123.x: Poverty measured by the Tendulkar line was stated to have fallen from 21.9 percent in 2011–12 to 2.3 percent in 2023–24.
123.tq: Distinguish the Tendulkar-line estimate from the MPI and World Bank estimates.
xs: Poverty on the **Tendulkar line** was **2.3 percent** in **2023-24** — option **(1)** (ES 2025-26).
**21.9%** was the earlier **2011-12** figure.
xa: Tendulkar 2004-05 estimate: **37.2%**.
Critics say the Tendulkar line is **too low**.
Income inequality is **rising** (World Inequality Database).

123.s:
Match List-I (Poverty estimation group) with List-II (Method):
List-I | List-II
a. Y.K. Alagh Task Force | i. Calories only: 2,400 rural, 2,100 urban
b. Lakdawala Expert Group | ii. Dropped the calorie anchor; Mixed Reference Period
c. Tendulkar Expert Group | iii. Food plus non-food needs such as housing and transport
d. Rangarajan Expert Group | iv. State-specific lines using CPI-AL and CPI-IW
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Alagh (1979) – calorie norms 2,400/2,100; Lakdawala (1993) – State-specific lines, CPI-AL rural and CPI-IW urban; Tendulkar (2009) – dropped calorie anchor, MRP, urban basket for both, health and education; Rangarajan (2014) – food + non-food.

123.s:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Task):
List-I | List-II
a. Dandekar and Rath (1971) | i. Method of the rural BPL census
b. Y.K. Alagh Task Force (1979) | ii. Identifying urban BPL households
c. S.R. Hashim Expert Group (2009) | iii. Calorie-based spending norm
d. N.C. Saxena Expert Group (2009) | iv. First poverty-line study, 2,250 calories
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Dandekar & Rath (1971) – first poverty-line study (2,250 calories); Alagh Task Force (1979) – spending needed to buy 2,400/2,100 calories; S.R. Hashim (2009) – urban BPL identification; N.C. Saxena (2009) – rural BPL census method.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tendulkar Expert Group was set up in 2005.
2. By the Tendulkar method, poverty was 37.2% in 2004-05 and 21.9% in 2011-12.
3. The Tendulkar Expert Group fixed calorie norms of 2,400 for rural and 2,100 for urban areas.
4. The Lakdawala method gave a poverty estimate of 27.5% for 2004-05.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 2,400/2,100 calorie norms belong to the Alagh Task Force; the Tendulkar group dropped the calorie anchor.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rangarajan Expert Group:
1. It was set up in 2012 and reported in 2014.
2. Its poverty lines for 2011-12 were ₹32 per day in rural and ₹47 per day in urban areas.
3. Its monthly per capita lines for 2011-12 were ₹972 urban and ₹1,407 rural.
4. In October 2025 NITI Aayog updated the Rangarajan line using HCES 2022-23.
How many of the above statements are correct?
123.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the lines were ₹972 rural and ₹1,407 urban (reversed). 4 is wrong: the update (Oct 2025) was by the RBI, not NITI Aayog.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In India, Scheduled Tribes have the highest incidence of poverty, followed by Scheduled Castes.
Reason (R): Discrimination and social exclusion, landlessness and remoteness keep these groups poor.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: Both are true and R explains A: the notes give discrimination, social exclusion, landlessness and remoteness as the cause of the ST > SC > others order.

123.s:
Consider the following statements (2025-26 data):
1. Informal employment in rural Andhra Pradesh is 62.3%.
2. Gig workers form about 12% of India's workforce.
3. India's social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to 64.3% in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: gig workers form a little over 2% of the workforce.

124.s: These rights enable men to have a reasonable and legal source of livelihood.
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Education & Data Processing Sec
124.x: Economic rights secure a person a reasonable and legal source of livelihood (work, wages, leisure). Liberty and religion are civil rights; education is a social-cultural right.

124.s: What is Magna Carta?
o: Charter of liberties signed by English King in AD 1215
124.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
124.x: Magna Carta (1215) is the charter of liberties signed by King John of England, the first document of the human-rights campaign. The other options are word-play distractors.

124.s: The Doctrine of Natural Rights as a part of the proposal for the spread of human rights was popularised by
124.x: John Locke popularised the doctrine of natural rights (life, liberty, property). Rousseau is known for the social contract and general will; Plato and Aristotle predate the natural-rights doctrine.

124.s: John Locke gave birth to the concept of human rights. He was a
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Animal Husbandry Assistant 2019
124.x: John Locke was an English (British) political thinker of the 17th century, author of the Two Treatises of Government. He was not American, German or French.

124.s: "Human rights serve as the protective Shield to the individuals whenever the state attempts to interfere with the civil liberties of individuals". This was stated by
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Village Sericulture Assistant 2019
124.x: The idea of rights as a protective shield (trumps) for the individual against State interference with civil liberties is Ronald Dworkin's; 'Ronald Darwin' is a garbled print of his name. Rousseau, Plato and Aristotle did not frame rights this way.

124.s: Name the French revolutionary who wrote ‘Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen’.
124.x: Olympe de Gouges wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen (1791) during the French Revolution. Mary Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman; Robespierre was a revolutionary leader.

124.s: The theory of ‘Natural Rights’ was propounded by
124.x: John Locke propounded the theory of natural rights to life, liberty and property. Hobbes, Bentham (utilitarianism) and Marx are linked to other theories.

124.s:
Which of the following is/are instance(s) of violation of human rights?

I. A person was detained by the security forces while going for casting vote in Parliamentary Election.

II. A civilian was killed by the Army while undertaking combing operation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
124.x: Both are violations: detaining a person on the way to vote denies political participation, and killing a civilian in a combing operation violates the right to life.

124.s: The concept of Human Rights primarily emphasizes on
o: Dignity of Man as a Human Being
124.x: Human rights rest on the dignity of man as a human being; the UDHR Preamble begins with the inherent dignity and equal rights of all. Property, equality and religion are particular rights, not the core idea.

124.s: Take the case of dignity and equal rights for women. How do democrates help?
o: Women in democracies have equal degree of political representation in legislature.
Women in democracies have guaranteed rights and are always treated with respect.
Women in democracies are not subjected to sex discrimination in most aspects of social life.
In democracies, the principle of equality is accepted as legal norm, which makes it easier to guarantee their freedom and dignity.
124.x: In democracies equality is accepted as a legal norm, which makes it easier to guarantee women's freedom and dignity. The other options overstate: democracies do not ensure equal representation or that women are always respected.

124.s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rights are claims of the State against the citizens
Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the
Rights are claims of the citizens against the State
Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many
124.x: Rights are claims of the citizens against the State: they limit State power and guarantee against State action. They are not claims of the State or privileges of a few.

124.s: 'Respect for human rights and responsibilities' is a
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Education & Data Processing Sec
124.x: Respect for human rights and responsibilities is a constitutional value, flowing from the Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties, rather than a merely civic, religious or economic value.

124.s: The person who described Human Rights as the new standards of civilisation.
124.x: Jack Donnelly described human rights as 'a new standard of civilization' (International Affairs, 1998); 'John Dowski' is a garbled print of his name. Plato, Aristotle and Rousseau did not use the phrase.

124.s: Who made the famous statement "Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains."?
124.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
124.x: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains' opens Rousseau's The Social Contract (1762); Locke, Mirabeau and Voltaire did not write it.

124.s: What Rights are Human Rights ?
o: Rights which are provided by Constitution of India
Rights provided to all human beings by nature
124.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Welfare & Development Secret
124.x: Human rights are the rights all human beings have by nature, simply as humans. Constitutional or fundamental rights are those a State grants; mere desires are not rights.

124.s: Right to vote is:
124.x: The right to vote is a political right (participation in government). In India it is a statutory right (Sec. 62, RP Act 1951), not a Fundamental Right.

124.s: Social rights will not include
124.x: Social rights protect groups such as women, children and Adivasis; 'care for political section' is not a social right (garbled option).

124.s:
Consider the following statements about human rights:
1. Human rights are inherent and inalienable to every human being.
2. In India every human right is also a Fundamental Right.
3. The Vienna Declaration (1993) affirmed that human rights are indivisible and interdependent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: every Fundamental Right is a human right, but not every human right is a Fundamental Right.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In India the right to vote is not a Fundamental Right.
Reason (R): The right to vote in India is a statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: Both are true and R explains A: the right to vote, a political right, is only a statutory right (Sec. 62, RP Act 1951), not part of Part III.

124.s:
Match List-I (Document / event) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Magna Carta | i. 1688
b. Glorious Revolution, England | ii. 1215
c. US Declaration of Independence | iii. 1776
d. French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen | iv. 1789
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Magna Carta – 1215 (King John); Glorious Revolution – 1688 (Bill of Rights 1689); US Declaration of Independence – 1776; French Declaration of the Rights of Man – 1789.

124.s:
Match List-I (Thinker) with List-II (Work / idea):
List-I | List-II
a. J.J. Rousseau | i. 'Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains'
b. Olympe de Gouges | ii. A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)
c. Mary Wollstonecraft | iii. Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen (1791)
d. John Locke | iv. Natural rights – life, liberty, property
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Rousseau – the chains line (Social Contract, 1762); Olympe de Gouges – Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791); Mary Wollstonecraft – A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792), not the 1791 Declaration; Locke – natural rights.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Civil Liberties Union was founded in 1946.
2. The Bhargava Commission (Andhra Pradesh, 1977) dealt with civil-liberties demands.
3. World Health Day is observed on 7 April and Labour Day on 1 May.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Indian Civil Liberties Union was founded on 24 August 1936 (Jawaharlal Nehru and others).

124.s: When is International Human Rights Day observed?
124.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
124.x: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the day the UNGA adopted the UDHR in 1948. 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti/Non-Violence Day, 14 November Children's Day in India.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights equates ___ with unemployment, sickness, disability and old age with the right to a standard of living adequate for the health and well-being of herself and of her family, including food, clothing, housing and medical care.
124.x: UDHR Art. 25(1) gives the right to security in the event of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood and old age, with an adequate standard of living. Divorce, adolescence and immigration are not listed there.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone's rights today
124.x: The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone's rights today
124.x: The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone’s rights today
124.x: Human Rights Day 2016 had the theme 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme; the others are not the 2016 theme.

124.s: When was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted by the United Nations?
124.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948 in Paris. 24 October 1945 is the date the UN came into being.

124.s: 10th December is celebrated as –
124.x: 10 December is Human Rights Day, marking the UDHR's adoption in 1948 (UNGA resolution 423(V), 1950). World Health Day is 7 April, UN Day 24 October, Labour Day 1 May.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by UN General Assembly, doesnot include which of the following?
o: Freedom of Adequate Standard of Living
124.x: The UDHR covers dignity, liberty and equality (Art. 1), the right to life (Art. 3) and an adequate standard of living (Art. 25), but not a right to universal basic income.

124.s: Which of the following is not considered to be one of the Human Rights listed by the United Nations?
124.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None of the above); it is added as option 5.
All four printed rights are in the UDHR: freedom and equality (Art. 1), life and liberty (Art. 3), education (Art. 26) and privacy (Art. 12: no arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home or correspondence). So none is outside the UN list (official JPSC key: Right to Privacy).

124.s: How many Articles are there in ‘Universal Declaration of Human Rights’?
124.x: The UDHR has a Preamble and 30 Articles.

124.s: Which day is the ‘International Human Rights Day’?
124.x: Human Rights Day is 10 December, the day the UDHR was adopted in 1948. 24 October is UN Day.

124.s: When is the International Child Rights Day is celebrated?
124.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
124.x: Universal (International) Children's Day is 20 November, the date the UNGA adopted the Declaration (1959) and the Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989). 14 November is Children's Day in India.

124.s: Which human rights document helps to guide the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Agenda?
124.x: The UDHR covers civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights and guides the SDGs Agenda. The Paris Agreement (climate), Magna Carta and NAFTA (trade) are not its guide.

124.s: Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a
o: Declaration adopted by several Nations at an International Conference
124.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
124.x: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly as resolution 217 A on 10 December 1948; it is a declaration, not a treaty.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights covers which rights?
o: Civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights
Only economic, social and cultural rights
124.x: The UDHR covers all five categories of rights, though it is not a treaty and is not legally binding as one.
xa: Binding covenants came later: **ICCPR** and **ICESCR** (adopted **16 Dec 1966**).
**International Bill of Human Rights** = **UDHR + ICCPR + ICESCR** + optional protocols.
Adopted by the **UNGA** on **10 December 1948**.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about the UDHR:
1. It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in Paris.
2. The committee that drafted it was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.
3. Human Rights Day on 10 December was fixed by UNGA resolution 423(V) in 1948.
4. It consists of a Preamble and 30 articles.
How many of the above statements are correct?
124.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: resolution 423(V) fixing Human Rights Day was passed in 1950, not 1948.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The UDHR is legally binding on all UN member States.
Reason (R): The UDHR is a declaration adopted by a UN General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: A is false: as a declaration the UDHR is not legally binding. R is true: it was adopted as a UNGA resolution (10 Dec 1948) and is not a treaty.

124.s:
Match List-I (UDHR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 3 | i. Work
b. Article 12 | ii. Life, liberty and security
c. Article 23 | iii. Education
d. Article 26 | iv. Privacy
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Art. 3 – life, liberty, security; Art. 12 – privacy (also ICCPR Art. 17); Art. 23 – work; Art. 26 – education.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.
2. The theme of Human Rights Day 2025 was 'Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials'.
3. Universal Children's Day on 20 November marks the adoption of the UNCRC in 1989.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now' was the 2024 theme; the 2016 theme was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'.

124.s: Amnesty International is
o: an agency of the United Nations to help refugees of civil wars
a non-governmental voluntary organisation to help very poor people
an inter-governmental agency to cater to medical emergencies in war-ravaged regions
124.x: Amnesty International (London, 1961) is a global human rights movement, an NGO; it is not a UN refugee agency, a poverty-relief body or an inter-governmental medical agency.

124.s: Amnesty International is –
o: An agency of the United Nations to help refugees of
A non-governmental voluntary organization to help
An inter-governmental agency to cater to medical
124.x: Amnesty International is a global movement campaigning against human-rights abuses, founded in 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson, headquartered in London. It is not a UN or inter-governmental agency.

124.s: Who is the winner of United Nations Human Rights Prize 2018 in the field of activities for the rights of Women and Girls?
o: All three Ms. Joenia Wapichana, Ms. Asma Jahangir and Ms. Rebeca Gyumi
124.x: The 2018 UN Human Rights Prize went to Rebeca Gyumi (Tanzania) for the rights of women and girls; Asma Jahangir (posthumous) and Joenia Wapichana also won, but in other fields (Front Line Defenders was the fourth).

124.s: Which one is not related to United Nations?
124.x: The General Assembly, ICJ and Trusteeship Council are principal UN organs; Amnesty International is an NGO with no UN status.

124.s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Organisation)
List-II (Associated Convention / Person / Place / Headquarters)
A. Amnesty International
1. Viskuli
B. Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
2. Paris
C. Danube Commission
3. Peter Benenson
D. European Space Agency
4. Belgrade Convention Which of the following is correctly matched?
124.x: Amnesty International – Peter Benenson (A-3); CIS – Viskuli agreement, Belarus (B-1); Danube Commission – Belgrade Convention (C-4); European Space Agency – Paris HQ (D-2).

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by Peter Benenson.
2. Amnesty International received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987.
3. Human Rights Watch is a New York-based NGO.
4. The UN Human Rights Prize is given by the UNGA, usually every five years, since 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Amnesty received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

124.s: In July 2022, UN General Assembly adopted a historic resolution declaring access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment, a universal _______.
124.x: On 28 July 2022 the UNGA recognised access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment as a universal human right.

124.s: United Nations Human Rights Council(UNHRC) has 47 UN member states with specific number of seats allotted for each five regions of the globe. How many seats are allotted for Asia-Pacific States.
124.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
124.x: Of the UN Human Rights Council's 47 seats, the Asia-Pacific group holds 13 (as does Africa); Latin America 8, Western Europe and Others 7, Eastern Europe 6.

124.s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Declaration on the Right to Development?
124.x: The right to development was recognised by a UNGA Declaration in 1986.

124.s:
Match the following regional groups with their seats in the UN Human Rights Council:
List-I
A. Africa
B. Latin America and Caribbean
C. Western Europe and Others
D. Eastern Europe
List-II
1. 6
2. 7
3. 8
4. 13
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
124.x: Of the 47 seats, Africa has 13, Latin America and Caribbean 8, Western Europe and Others 7 and Eastern Europe 6.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It was set up in 2006 in place of the UN Commission on Human Rights and is based in Geneva.
2. Its 47 members are elected by the UNGA for four-year terms.
3. A member can serve at most two consecutive terms.
4. A member can be suspended by a two-thirds vote of the UNGA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: HRC members serve three-year terms.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Universal Periodic Review, a peer review of every UN member's record, began in 2008 in cycles of about 4.5 years.
2. Special rapporteurs under the special procedures are paid UN staff.
3. The OHCHR was set up in 1993 after the Vienna Conference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Paris Principles were drafted in Paris in October 1991 and adopted by the UNGA in 1993.
2. The Paris Principles require an NHRI to depend on the executive for investigations.
3. GANHRI accredits NHRIs through its Sub-Committee on Accreditation; 'A' status means fully compliant.
4. India's NHRC is a constitutional NHRI.
How many of the above statements are correct?
124.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Principles require independence, autonomy and powers to investigate. 4 is wrong: the NHRC (1993) is a statutory body under the PHRA 1993.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment is a third-generation (collective) human right.
Reason (R): The UN General Assembly recognised the Right to Water and Sanitation on 28 July 2010.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: Both are true – a healthy environment is a collective, third-generation right (UNGA recognition 28 July 2022), and water and sanitation was recognised on 28 July 2010 – but R does not explain A.

124.s: Which one of the following is considered to be the second generation of Human Rights ?
124.x:
Most books and keys: Right to Education. Strictly: the Right to Work (ICESCR Art. 6) is equally a second-generation right, so that option is also correct; the stem is loose (general knowledge, not checked).
In Vasak's scheme the second generation (equality) covers economic, social and cultural rights, so the Right to Education is the expected answer. Liberty and Equality before law are first-generation rights.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about the generations of human rights:
1. Karel Vasak proposed the three-generation classification in 1977.
2. Third-generation rights are linked with the ideal of fraternity.
3. Eradication of social discrimination is a first-generation right.
4. Social security is a second-generation right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: eradication of social discrimination is a second-generation (equality) right; first-generation rights are civil and political.

124.s: Child Rights are protected in Article_______of ICCPR.
124.x: Article 24 of the ICCPR protects the rights of the child (protection, name, nationality). Art. 21 is peaceful assembly and Art. 23 family; Art. 24 of the Indian Constitution also concerns children (child labour).

124.s: In which year was the Optional Protocol to the ICESCR adopted?
124.x: The ICESCR Optional Protocol was adopted in 2008; 1976 is when the two Covenants entered into force.

124.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is associated with which treaty and what change in the number of recognised disabilities?
124.x: The CRPD concerns persons with disabilities and gave rise to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.
124.tq: Link the treaty, implementing legislation and numerical change as one factual chain.
xs: The **RPwD Act, 2016** flows from the **CRPD** and raised recognised disabilities **from 7 to 21** — option **(4)**.
**CPED** is on **enforced disappearance** and **CEDAW** on **discrimination against women**; option (1) reverses the numbers.
xa: CRPD adopted **2006**; India **ratified 2007**.
**CPED** (**2006**) — India **signed 2007, not ratified**.
**CMW** (**1990**, migrant workers) — India **not signed**.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Bill of Human Rights comprises the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.
2. The ICCPR entered into force before the ICESCR.
3. India acceded to both Covenants in 1979 but has not signed the ICCPR First Optional Protocol.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the ICESCR entered into force first (3 Jan 1976), the ICCPR on 23 Mar 1976.

124.s:
Match List-I (ICCPR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 6 | i. Fair trial
b. Article 7 | ii. Life
c. Article 14 | iii. Freedom from torture
d. Article 19 | iv. Expression
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: ICCPR: Art. 6 – life; Art. 7 – no torture; Art. 14 – fair trial; Art. 19 – expression (privacy is Art. 17, child rights Art. 24).

124.s:
Match List-I (Convention) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. CERD | i. Persons with disabilities
b. CMW | ii. Enforced disappearance
c. CPED | iii. Migrant workers
d. CRPD | iv. Racial discrimination
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: CERD (1965) – racial discrimination, ratified by India 1968; CMW (1990) – migrant workers, not signed; CPED (2006) – enforced disappearance, signed 2007; CRPD (2006) – disabilities, ratified 2007.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about India and UN human rights treaties:
1. CEDAW was adopted in 1979 and ratified by India in 1993.
2. India ratified the Convention against Torture in 1997.
3. India acceded to the CRC on 11 December 1992.
How many of the above statements are correct?
124.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: India signed the CAT in 1997 but has not ratified it.

125.s: Article prohibits untouchability in any form in the Constitution
125.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 16 equality in public employment, Art. 19 the six freedoms.

125.s: The Article in which 'Prohibition of Untouchability' is incorporated
125.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 16 equality in public employment, Art. 19 the six freedoms.

125.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution Guarantees the Right to Equality?
125.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
125.x: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws. Art. 19 gives the six freedoms, Art. 21 life and liberty, Art. 25 freedom of religion.

125.s: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution professes that State shall not deny any person 'Equality before the law'?
125.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
125.x: Article 14: the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. Arts. 11-13 deal with citizenship law, the definition of State and laws inconsistent with FRs.

125.s: ___ prohibits traffic in human beings and 'begar' and other similar forms of forced labour.
125.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
125.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour. Art. 27 is about taxes for religion, Art. 33 about armed forces, Art. 37 about DPSP enforceability.

125.s: Which Article of Indian Constitution says that 'untouchability' is abolished?
125.x: Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability. Art. 18 abolishes titles, Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 3 is about new States.

125.s: Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits
o: Traffic in human beings and forced labour
125.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar). Untouchability is Art. 17; discrimination is barred by Art. 15.

125.s:
Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India?
1. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
2. Abolition of untouchability
3. Protection of the interests of minorities
4. Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
125.x: The Right against Exploitation is Arts. 23 (traffic and forced labour) and 24 (no child below 14 in factories, mines). Untouchability (Art. 17) is under the Right to Equality and minorities are under Arts. 29-30, so 1 and 4 only.

125.s: Which one of the following is a fundamental right under the constitution of India and a human right as well
125.x: Art. 21A makes education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right as well as a human right (UDHR Art. 26). Information is statutory, and housing and a right to die are not Fundamental Rights.

125.s: Which one of the following is a human right as well as a fundamental right under the Constitution of India?
125.x: Art. 21A makes education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right as well as a human right. Information, work and housing are not Fundamental Rights.

125.s: The bonded labour (Abolition) Act, 1976 is related to
125.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 was enacted under Article 23, which prohibits begar and forced labour. Art. 24 is child labour, Arts. 25 and 27 are religion.

125.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 23 – Prohibition of employment of children in factories
Article 22 – Protection against arrest and detention
Article 20 – Protection in respect of conviction for offences
Article 24 – Prohibition of employment of children in factories
125.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour; child employment in factories is Article 24.
n: Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 23 prohibits forced labour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 24 prohibits the employment of children. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xa: **Article 21**: **life and personal liberty**.
**Bonded labour** falls under **Art. 23**.
Article 24: no child below **14** in factories, mines, hazardous work.

125.s: Who called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
125.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) the heart and soul of the Constitution.

125.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 15(4), enabling special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs?
125.x: Article 15(4) was added by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951.

125.s:
Match List-I (Article of the Constitution) with List-II (Parallel UDHR Article):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 14 | i. Article 8
b. Article 21 | ii. Article 26
c. Article 32 | iii. Article 7
d. Article 21A | iv. Article 3
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Art. 14 (equality before law) – UDHR Art. 7; Art. 21 (life, liberty) – UDHR Art. 3; Art. 32 (remedies) – UDHR Art. 8; Art. 21A (education) – UDHR Art. 26.

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The freedoms under Article 19 are available only to citizens.
2. Article 21 is available to both citizens and foreigners.
3. Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
4. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 16 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: Article 24 bars children below 14 years, not 16.

125.s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Provision):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 12 | i. Organisation of village panchayats (DPSP)
b. Article 13 | ii. Defines 'State' for the Fundamental Rights
c. Article 40 | iii. Laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void
d. Article 15(4) | iv. Special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Art. 12 – definition of 'State'; Art. 13 – laws inconsistent with FRs void (judicial review); Art. 40 – village panchayats, a DPSP; Art. 15(4) – special provisions, added by the First Amendment.

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Right to Information is expressly listed as a Fundamental Right in Part III.
Reason (R): The Right to Information is a statutory right under the RTI Act, 2005, also read into Article 19(1)(a).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
125.x: A is false: RTI is not an express Fundamental Right. R is true: it is statutory (RTI Act 2005) and has been read into Art. 19(1)(a).

125.s: The Indian Union Parliament approved The Protection of Human Right Act in
125.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Animal Husbandry Assistant 2019
125.x: Parliament passed the Protection of Human Rights Act in 1993 (deemed in force from 28 Sept 1993; NHRC constituted 12 Oct 1993).

125.s: Every member of the Commission, Sate Commission and every officer appointed or authorized by the Commission or State Commission to exercise functions under the Protection of Human Rights Act is to be deemed
125.x: Under Section 39 of the PHRA, every member and officer of the Commission or a State Commission is deemed a public servant within Sec. 21 IPC.

125.s: In the definition of armed forces under the Protection of Human Rights Act, which of the following is not included?
125.x: Under the PHRA, 'armed forces' means the naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union; armed forces of the State are not included.

125.s: An advocate may be specified by the State Government for the purpose of conducting of cases in Human Rights courts as Special Public Prosecutor who has been in practice for not less than :
125.x: Under Section 31 of the PHRA, the State Government may appoint as Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court an advocate with not less than seven years' practice.

125.s: In which Section of the Human Rights Protection Act, 1993 is ‘Public Servant’ defined?
125.x: Section 2(1)(m) of the PHRA defines 'public servant' (by reference to Sec. 21 IPC), so Section 2(M) is correct. Sec. 2(1)(a) defines armed forces, Sec. 2(1)(h) Member.

125.s: Under which Article of the Constitution the Protection of Human Rights Ordinance was issued by the President in 1993?
125.x: The President promulgated the Protection of Human Rights Ordinance, 1993 under Article 123 (ordinance power) on 28 September 1993. Art. 124 is the Supreme Court, Arts. 125 and 127 judges' salaries and ad hoc judges.

125.s: In relation to offences described under Section 175, Section 178, Section 179, Section 180 or Section 228 of the Indian Penal Code, the Human Rights Commission is to be deemed
125.x: When an offence under IPC sections 175, 178, 179, 180 or 228 is committed before it, the Commission is deemed a civil court (Sec. 13 PHRA) and may forward the case to a Magistrate.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
1. The NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993.
2. The Act is deemed to have come into force on 28 September 1993, though it received assent in January 1994.
3. Under its three-tier set-up, Human Rights Courts function at the State level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the tiers are NHRC (national), SHRC (State) and Human Rights Courts (district).

125.s:
Match List-I (Section of the PHRA, 1993) with List-II (Defines):
List-I | List-II
a. Section 2(1)(a) | i. Human rights
b. Section 2(1)(d) | ii. International Covenants
c. Section 2(1)(f) | iii. Armed forces
d. Section 2(1)(m) | iv. Public servant
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: 2(1)(a) – armed forces (Union forces; State armed police not included); 2(1)(d) – human rights; 2(1)(f) – International Covenants (ICCPR + ICESCR); 2(1)(m) – public servant.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about the PHRA, 1993:
1. A Human Rights Court is a Court of Session notified by the State Government with the concurrence of the High Court Chief Justice.
2. A Special Public Prosecutor must be an advocate with at least 10 years' practice.
3. 'Public servant' has the meaning in Sec. 21 IPC, now Sec. 2(28) of the BNS.
4. Commission proceedings are judicial proceedings for IPC Sections 193 and 228.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Sec. 31 requires an advocate of at least 7 years' practice.

125.s: ____ constitutes the right to get pollution-free water and air. It ensures the right to 'live' is not merely confined to physical existence, but it includes within its ambit right to live with human dignity.
125.x: Article 21 has been read to include a decent environment with pollution-free water and air and the right to live with human dignity (Maneka Gandhi). Arts. 20, 22 and 23 deal with conviction, arrest and exploitation.

125.s: The Supreme Court of India has expanded the meaning of the Right to Life to include the following derivative rights. Which one among the following is not included in the court’s definition?
o: Right to Food and Adequate Livelihood
Right to Live in a Healthy Environment
125.x:
Most books and keys: Right to Health and Information. Strictly: Laxmikanth lists both the right to health and the right to information among rights read into Art. 21, so every option is in the court's definition (Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01) p.148-149).
The expected answer is 'Right to Health and Information', on the view that information flows mainly from Art. 19(1)(a); food/livelihood, education and a healthy environment are classic Art. 21 readings.

125.s:
Which of the following statements are true for the Fundamental Right to Life and Personal Liberty as guaranteed under Article-21 of the Constitution of India?

I. The Right is available to citizens as well as aliens.

II. It covers protection against arbitrary executive and legislative action.

III. It includes the right to live with human dignity.

IV. It can be taken away according to the procedure established by law.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
125.x: All four hold: Art. 21 extends to citizens and aliens; after Maneka Gandhi it guards against arbitrary executive and legislative action; it includes life with dignity; and it can be curtailed only by procedure established by law.

125.s:
Match List-I (Right read into Article 21) with List-II (Case):
List-I | List-II
a. Free legal aid | i. M.H. Hoskot (1978)
b. Speedy trial | ii. K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)
c. Livelihood | iii. Olga Tellis (1985)
d. Privacy | iv. Hussainara Khatoon (1979)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Legal aid – M.H. Hoskot (1978); speedy trial – Hussainara Khatoon (1979); livelihood – Olga Tellis (1985); privacy – K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The safeguards in D.K. Basu (1997) relate mainly to bail for under-trial prisoners.
2. In Francis Coralie (1981) the Supreme Court held that the right to life includes the right to live with human dignity.
3. The right to a clean environment was read into Article 21 in Subhash Kumar (1991).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: D.K. Basu laid down safeguards for persons during arrest and custodial detention.

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In Maneka Gandhi (1978) the protection of Article 21 was extended against arbitrary legislative action as well as executive action.
Reason (R): The Court held that the procedure depriving a person of life or liberty must be fair, just and reasonable.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
125.x: Both are true and R explains A: by requiring the law's procedure itself to be fair, just and reasonable, Maneka Gandhi reversed the narrow A.K. Gopalan (1950) view that Art. 21 protected only against executive action.

125.s: Fundamental Duties enshrined in the Constitution are in consonance with
125.x: The Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, 42nd Amendment 1976) are in consonance with the UDHR, whose Art. 29 says everyone has duties to the community. CEDAW, WIPO and WTO have no such link.

125.s:
Other than the Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect/reflects the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)?
1. Preamble
2. Directive Principles of State Policy
3. Fundamental duties
Select the correct answer using the given code below:
125.x: The Preamble (justice, liberty, equality, dignity), the DPSPs (work, living wage, education, health) and the Fundamental Duties (UDHR Art. 29: duties to the community) all reflect the UDHR, so 1, 2 and 3.

125.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities?
125.x: Article 43 (DPSP) asks the State to secure a living wage, a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities. Art. 42 is humane conditions and maternity relief; Art. 39 livelihood and equal pay; Art. 40 panchayats.

125.s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Provision):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 42 | i. Living wage for workers
b. Article 43 | ii. Respect for international law and treaty obligations
c. Article 51(c) | iii. Renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
d. Article 51A(e) | iv. Humane conditions of work and maternity relief
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Art. 42 – humane conditions and maternity relief; Art. 43 – living wage, decent standard of life; Art. 51(c) – respect for international law (DPSP); Art. 51A(e) – Fundamental Duty on the dignity of women.

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws to implement international treaties.
2. The Vishaka guidelines (1997) relied substantially on the UNCRC.
3. In Guruvayur Devaswom (2003) it was held that courts may use international conventions.
4. The NCPCR was set up in 2007, after India acceded to the UNCRC in 1992.
How many of the above statements are correct?
125.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Vishaka relied on CEDAW, not the UNCRC.

125.s: Which of the following is not a Social Act?
125.x: MISA (1971, repealed 1977) was an internal-security (preventive detention) law, not a social Act. The Dowry, Protection of Civil Rights and Immoral Traffic Acts fight social evils.

125.s: In which year did the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 come into force?
125.x: The Domestic Violence Act was enacted in 2005 and came into force in 2006 (26 October 2006).
n: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act became effective in 1990. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was enacted in 2005. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act became effective in 2006. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]

125.s:
Match List-I (Act) with List-II (Year in force / enacted):
List-I | List-II
a. Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act | i. 1990
b. SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act | ii. 1976
c. Right to Information Act | iii. 2010
d. National Green Tribunal Act | iv. 2005
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Bonded Labour Act – 1976 (Ordinance 1975); SC/ST Atrocities Act – 1989, in force 30 Jan 1990; RTI – in force 12 Oct 2005; NGT Act – 2010.

125.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MISA was enacted in 1971 and repealed in 1977.
2. Under the Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026, the identity certificate is issued by the National Council for Transgender Persons.
3. The Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 bans sewer cleaning without protective gear and requires a latrine survey within three years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: under the 2026 amendment the District Magistrate certifies, on medical-board advice.

125.s:
Match List-I (Act) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Protection of Civil Rights Act | i. 1961
b. Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act | ii. 2005
c. Dowry Prohibition Act | iii. 1955
d. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act | iv. 1956
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
125.x: Protection of Civil Rights – 1955; Immoral Traffic Prevention – 1956; Dowry Prohibition – 1961; Domestic Violence – 2005 (in force 26 Oct 2006).

126.s:
Which of the following statements/statements is/are correct in relation to the Human Rights Commissions in India?

I. The role to undertake functions relating to human rights in the Union Territory of Ladakh may be conferred upon a State Human Rights Commission by the Central Government.

II. Only 2 persons can be appointed as members of the National Human Rights Commission under the category of possessing knowledge or practical experience with respect to human rights.

III. The President can remove the Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission on the ground of proved misbehaviour. However, the President has to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in this matter.

IV. The National Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into any matter after the expiry of two years from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
126.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Only III); it is added as option 5.
Only III is correct: SHRC members are removed only by the President, and for proved misbehaviour only after a Supreme Court inquiry on the President's reference. I is wrong (UT functions cannot go to an SHRC for Delhi, J&K or Ladakh), II is wrong (three human-rights members since 2019), IV is wrong (time bar is one year). (Printed key: None.)

126.s: Who appoints the State Human Rights Commission?
126.src: Assistant BC, Social, Tribal Welfare Officer Screening Test
126.x: SHRC Chairperson and members are appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Chief Minister.

126.s: The member of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by the
126.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Grade-IV Mains Paper-I 2
126.x: Though appointed by the Governor, the Chairperson or a member of an SHRC can be removed only by the President.

126.s: Chairperson and Members of the State Human Rights Commission are appointed by.
o: Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned State
126.x: SHRC Chairperson and members are appointed by the Governor, though removal is only by the President.

126.s: A Sitting Judge of the High Court or a Sitting District Judge can be appointed as a member of the State Human Rights Commission after consultation with?
o: the Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned
the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India
126.x: A sitting HC Judge or sitting District Judge can be appointed to an SHRC only after consulting the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State concerned.

126.s: Chairperson and members of State Human Rights Commission are appointed by –
126.x: The SHRC Chairperson and members are appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Chief Minister.

126.s: In the event of occurrence of any vacancy in the Office of the Chairperson of the State Commission, who can authorize one of the members to act as Chairperson?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Chairperson of the National Human Rights
126.x: If the SHRC Chairperson's office falls vacant, the Governor may authorise one of the members to act as Chairperson.

126.s: The State Commission submits its annual report to the?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
126.x: The SHRC submits its annual or special reports to the State Government, which lays them before the State Legislature with a memorandum of action taken.

126.s: Who presides over the committee constituted for the appointment of members of the State Human Rights Commission?
126.x: Under Section 22, the committee recommending SHRC appointments is headed by the Chief Minister; the Governor appoints on its recommendation.

126.s: Which one of the following is not the function of the State Human Rights Commission?
o: Enquire suo-moto the violation of Human Rights
Review the protection of Human Rights
To punish for the violation of Human Rights
126.x: An SHRC can inquire suo motu, visit jails and review safeguards, but it cannot punish violators; it only recommends.

126.s: On completion of an inquiry the State Human Rights Commission may
o: issue orders for payment or damages to the complainant/victim
it may recommend to the concerned Government or authority to pay damages
it cannot initiate any action for compensation
it has only a fact finding mission
126.x: After an inquiry, an SHRC may only recommend that the State Government or authority pay compensation or damages; it cannot order payment itself.

126.s:
Consider the following statements labelled
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) with respect to the State Human Rights Commission and select the correct option.
Assertion (A): State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) can inquire into violation of human rights only in respect of subjects mentioned in the State List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The functions relating to human rights in the case of the union territory of Delhi are to be dealt with by the National Human Rights Commission.
o: A and R both are true, and R is the correct explanation for A.
A and R both are true, and R is the NOT the correct explanation for A.
A is correct, R is incorrect.
A is incorrect, R is correct.
126.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
126.x: A is false: an SHRC covers subjects in the State List and the Concurrent List, not the State List alone. R is true: human-rights functions for Delhi are dealt with by the NHRC.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC and SHRCs:
1. Both Chairpersons are removed by the President.
2. Both Chairpersons are appointed by the President.
3. The NHRC Chairperson resigns to the President and the SHRC Chairperson to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Both chairs are removed by the President, but the SHRC chair is appointed by the Governor, so statement 2 is wrong.

126.s: After the 2019 change, which body handles the human-rights functions relating to Delhi?
o: An SHRC on which the Centre confers them
126.x: The Centre may confer a Union Territory's human-rights functions on an SHRC, but Delhi's are handled by the NHRC itself.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about State Human Rights Commissions:
1. Constituting an SHRC is optional for a State Government.
2. The 2019 amendment cut the SHRC's strength from five to three.
3. Since 2019 a High Court Judge, besides a retired HC Chief Justice, can chair an SHRC.
4. In a bicameral State, the Chairman and the Leader of Opposition of the Legislative Council join the selection committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the SHRC was cut from five to three members by the 2006 amendment, not 2019.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about an SHRC:
1. Its Chairperson resigns to the Governor.
2. Its annual report goes to the State Government and is laid before the State Legislature with a memorandum of action taken.
3. It inquires only into subjects in the State List.
4. It does not inquire into a matter already being inquired into by the NHRC.
How many of the above statements are correct?
126.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: an SHRC covers subjects in both the State List and the Concurrent List.

126.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): A State Human Rights Commission can punish those who violate human rights.
Reason (R): An SHRC can only recommend compensation or damages to the Government.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
126.x: A is false: an SHRC, like the NHRC, cannot punish; its recommendations are not executable as decrees. R is true: on inquiry it may only recommend compensation or damages to the Government or authority.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh SHRC:
1. It was constituted by the AP Government under the PHRA, 1993.
2. Its headquarters is at Kurnool.
3. It has had a full-time Chairperson continuously since 2021.
4. In the Gade Sai Krishna custodial death (June 2026), the NHRC sought reports from the AP SHRC, the DGP and the Chief Secretary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the AP SHRC was reported to be without a Chairperson since March 2024.

126.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Human Rights Commission?

I. The National Human Rights Commission is a constitutional body.

II. It was established in 1994 under a legislation enacted by the Parliament, namely, the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1994.
126.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
126.x: Both are false: the NHRC is a statutory, not constitutional, body, and it was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (not 1994).

126.s: When was the Human Rights Commission of India constituted?
126.x: The NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

126.s: Which statement is true in relation to the Protection of Human Rights Act?
o: The Act came into force on 23rd September, 1993
The Act came into force on 28th September, 1993
The Act came into force on 23rd September, 1995
The Act came into force on 28th September, 1995
126.x: The Protection of Human Rights Act is deemed to have come into force on 28 September 1993, the date of the ordinance, and extends to the whole of India.

126.s: When did the Protection of Human Rights Act come into force in India?
