2. It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in 2015.
3. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 came into force on 10 January 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 2014 Bill was passed only by the Rajya Sabha (April 2015) – the first private member's Bill passed there in over four decades – and not by the Lok Sabha.

143.s:
With reference to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, consider the following statements:

3. Offences such as forced labour or abuse of transgender persons carry 6 months to 2 years' imprisonment and fine.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
143.x: Both true and R explains A: NALSA recognised self-identification; the amendment omits Sec. 4(2) (self-perceived identity) – it was challenged by Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel.

143.s:

143.x: Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: the Council is chaired by the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, and non-official members serve 3 years.

143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2019 Amendment Bill lapsed, so the Rs 10,000 cap remains.

143.x: All the statements are correct: Entry 24 of the Concurrent List covers invalidity and old age pensions; NSAP rests on Arts. 41 and 42; Himachal Pradesh's 2001 Act preceded the central 2007 Act.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
143.x: A is false: the SACRED portal is for re-employment of senior citizens. R is true: AVYAY is an umbrella of 4 components (including RVY, launched at Nellore in April 2017).

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding minorities in India:

1. The President of India has the power to declare any community as a minority.

4. Only linguistic minorities are recognized under the Indian Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
144.x: Only statement 2 is right: Art. 29 protects both religious and linguistic minorities. Minorities are notified by the Central Government (not the President), the NCM is statutory (1992 Act, not Art. 350B), and religious minorities are recognised too.

144.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the educational rights of religious minorities?
144.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
144.x: Article 30 gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions; Art. 29 covers language, script and culture.

144.s: Which article of the Indian constitution specifically a fundamental right that protects cultural rights of the people?
144.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
144.x: Article 29 protects the right of any section of citizens to conserve its distinct language, script or culture, which makes it the cultural-rights article; Art. 30 is about educational institutions.

144.s: The right to conserve distinct language, script or culture is mentioned in this article of the Constitution:
144.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screening T
144.x: Article 29(1) protects the right to conserve a distinct language, script or culture; Arts. 350, 350A and 351 deal with grievance language, mother-tongue teaching and Hindi.

144.s: "No citizen shall be denied admission in any educational institution maintained by the state or receiving aid out of state fund on grounds of religion, race, caste, language or any of them." It had been stated in which article of the constitution?
144.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
144.x: Article 29(2) bars denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste or language; 30(1) is the minorities' right to set up institutions.

144.x: Article 350B provides a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, so it safeguards linguistic minorities.

144.s: According to which article, the right of minorities to establish and administer minorities educational institutions?
144.x: Article 30(1): all minorities, religious or linguistic, may establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Article 29 is about conserving language, script and culture.

144.s:
Match
List I (Article of Indian Constitution) with
List II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Article of Indian Constitution)
A. Article 16(2)
B. Article 29(2)
C. Article 30(1)
D. Article 31(1)
List II (Provisions)
1. No person shall be deprived of his property save by the authority of law
2. No person can be discriminated against in the matter of public appointment on the ground of race, religion or caste
3. All minorities whether based on religion or language shall have the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice
4. No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State, or receiving State aid, on grounds of religion, race, caste, language or any of them
Codes:
144.x: 16(2) is no discrimination in public employment (2), 29(2) no denial of admission (4), 30(1) minorities' institutions (3) and old 31(1) no deprivation of property save by law (1), giving A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1.

144.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the 'Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice'?
144.x: Article 30 protects the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions; Art. 29 protects the interests of minorities, Art. 26 religious affairs and Art. 19 freedoms.

144.s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
144.x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
144.tq: Apply the factual situation to the specific clause dealing with State aid to minority-managed institutions.
xs: **Article 30(2)** — the State shall not discriminate against **minority-managed** institutions in **granting aid** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 29(1)** is about conserving language/culture, **29(2)** about admission, and **350A** about mother-tongue primary instruction.
xa: **Art. 30(1)** covers **all minorities, religious or linguistic** — the "Charter of Education Rights".
**Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment**.

b. Article 29(2)
c. Article 30(1A)

144.x: Section 2(c) of the NCM Act 1992 defines a minority as a community notified as such by the Central Government.

144.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
144.x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.
144.tq: Match the statutory provision with the specific constitutional criticism rather than a broader unrelated power.
xs: Critics say **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre **"unbridled power"** to **notify minorities** — option **(1)**.
It sits uneasily with **T.M.A. Pai (2002)**, which made the **State** the unit for minority status.
xa: The NCM Act does not define minority; a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
States may notify their own minorities — **Jains** in **11 States** before 2014.

144.s: Which is the largest notified minority community in India as per Census 2011?
144.x: Muslims form 14.2% of the population (Census 2011), the largest minority; Christians are 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The term 'minority' is defined in Article 366 of the Constitution.
2. The word 'minority' appears in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B.
3. Under Section 2(c) of the NCM Act, 1992, a minority is a community notified as such by the Central Government.
4. After the T.M.A. Pai case (2002), minority status is decided with reference to the national population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 'Minority' is not defined in the Constitution (1 wrong); T.M.A. Pai (11 judges) made the State the unit (4 wrong).

144.s:
Consider the following statements about notified minority communities:
1. The first five minority communities were notified in 1993.
2. Jains were notified as the sixth minority community in January 2014.
3. As per Census 2011, Sikhs are the second-largest minority community.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Two are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Christians (2.3%) are second largest after Muslims (14.2%); Sikhs are 1.7%.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jews are not a notified minority community in India.
2. The six notified minority communities together make up about 29% of India's population.
3. Eleven States had declared Jains a minority before the Centre notified them in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the six notified minorities together are about 19% of India's population.

144.s: State minority commission are set up by?
144.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
144.x: State Minorities Commissions are set up by the State Governments (under State laws), with offices in the State capitals.

144.s: The Minorities Commission consists of ____ members.
144.x:
Earlier app key: Five (the five Members besides the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson). Strictly the Commission has seven members (Laxmikanth Part 2 p.249).
The NCM has seven members: a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members (seven also before the 1995 amendment, as Chairperson plus six). "Five" counts only the Members other than the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson. (Earlier app key: Five.)

144.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
I. It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
II. Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities under "Minority" status, to date.
III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments. (B) I and II only
144.x: I and III are right: the NCM was set up under the 1992 Act and recommends effective implementation of safeguards by Central or State Governments. II is wrong because six communities are notified (Jains were added in 2014).

144.s: Who appoints the Chairman and Members of National Commission for minorities?
144.x: The Chairperson and Members of the NCM are nominated by the Central (Union) Government, not appointed by the President.

144.s: In India, how many states have set up State Minority Commissions?
144.x: By 2017 the Ministry of Minority Affairs told Parliament that 18 States/UTs had set up State Minorities Commissions; NextGen's older list names 15. (About 19 by 2026.)

144.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities
144.x: The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures; conducting elections to minority educational institutions is not one of its stated functions.
144.tq: Find the option that assigns an unrelated administrative function to the Commission.
xs: **Conducting elections to minority educational institutions** is NOT an NCM function — option **(1)**.
NCM functions: evaluate minorities' **development**, **monitor constitutional and legal safeguards**, look into **specific complaints**, recommend measures, commission studies.
xa: It has **powers of a civil court** while inquiring.
⚠ Minority status of institutions is decided by the **NCMEI**, not the NCM.

144.s: Who was the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
144.x: In July 2026 Harjit Singh Grewal was NCM Chairperson and Munawari Begum Vice-Chairperson; only 4 of 7 posts were filled.

144.s:
Match List I (Year) with List II (Milestone in the evolution of the NCM):
List I (Year)
a. 1978
b. 1992
c. 1995
d. 2006
List II (Milestone)
1. Ministry of Minority Affairs carved out of MoSJE
2. National Commission for Minorities Act enacted
3. Non-statutory Minorities Commission set up by MHA resolution
4. Amendment added the Vice-Chairperson
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: 1978 = non-statutory Minorities Commission (MHA resolution, 12 Jan 1978); 1992 = NCM Act; 1995 = Vice-Chairperson added; 2006 = Ministry of Minority Affairs created.

144.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory body and not a constitutional body.
2. It has seven members, of whom five including the Chairperson must be from minority communities.
3. Its members have a tenure of five years.
4. While inquiring into complaints it has the powers of a civil court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NCM members have a three-year tenure.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first chairman of the statutory National Commission for Minorities.
2. Haj management was given to the Ministry of Minority Affairs when the Ministry was created in 2006.
3. The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ministry was created in 2006 but Haj was added only in 2016.

144.s: If a person wants to set up a minority educational institute, out of the following, whose permission is mandatory?
o: Department of Education of the concerned State Government
National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions
144.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screening T
144.x: Under Section 10 of the NCMEI Act 2004, a person setting up a minority educational institution needs a No Objection Certificate from the competent authority of the State Government (its Department of Education). The NCMEI hears appeals and the NCM has no role in permission.

144.s: Which of the following is not correct in relation to the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions?
o: The Commission shall consist of Chairman and 3 members
To become Chairman of the Commission he shall be a member of a Minority community
Every member of the Commission shall hold office for term of 5 years
To remove the members of the commission parliament's Approval is required
144.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
144.x: The NCMEI has a Chairperson and three Members (as amended in 2010). The Chairperson must belong to a minority community, members serve 5 years, and they are removed by the Central Government, so no Parliamentary approval is needed.

144.s: Find out the wrong answer regarding the National Commission for Minority Education Institutions Act 2004.
o: If Application to establish a minority educational Institution is rejected, the competent Authority shall communicate the same to the applicant
Competent Authority has the discretion regarding the time limit for granting the permission to start Educational Institution
On application to establish a minority educational institution, 90 Days time is given to the competent Authority for giving permission
Within 90 days if the competent Authority doesn't grant or rejected, not communicated to the person who has applied, it shall be deemed that Competent Authority has granted No Objection Certificate
144.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
144.x: Section 10 of the NCMEI Act gives the competent authority no discretion over time: it must decide within 90 days and communicate any rejection, and if it does not, the NOC is deemed granted.

144.s: In an institution declared as a Minority Educational Institution by the Central Government, the percentage of reservation of seats for Scheduled Caste students is
144.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
144.x: Minority educational institutions are exempt from SC/ST/OBC reservation (Art. 15(5)), so the SC quota there is nil.

144.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions (NCMEI), consider the following statements:
1. It consists of a Chairperson and three Members nominated by the Central Government.
2. Its Chairperson must be a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
3. Its members have a five-year term.
4. It decides the minority status of educational institutions and issues minority certificates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chairperson must be from a minority community and a retired High Court judge.

144.s:
Match List I (Case) with List II (Held):
List I (Case)
a. In re Kerala Education Bill (1958)
b. St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974)
c. St. Stephen's College v. Delhi University (1992)
d. P.A. Inamdar (2005)
List II (Held)
1. Art. 143 reference; Art. 30 not absolute, reasonable conditions for aid
2. No State quota in unaided institutions
3. Regulation only for standards and excellence
4. Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to about 50%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: Kerala Education Bill = Presidential reference, Art. 30 not absolute; St. Xavier's = regulation only for standards; St. Stephen's = up to about 50% own-community preference; P.A. Inamdar = no State quota in unaided institutions.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court cases on minority institutions:
1. T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) was decided by an 11-judge Bench.
2. P.A. Inamdar (2005) was decided by a 9-judge Bench.
3. In Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) the Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a minority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: P.A. Inamdar was a 7-judge Bench.

144.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A State cannot impose SC/ST/OBC reservation on a minority educational institution.
Reason (R): Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, excludes minority educational institutions from reservation in admissions.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
144.x: Both true and R explains A: Art. 15(5) (and 15(6) for EWS) exclude minority educational institutions, so the SC quota in them is nil.

144.s: A High Level Committee for preparation of the Report on the Social, Economic and Educational status of the Muslim community of India was set up in 2005 and submitted its report in 2006. Who was the Chairman of the Committee?
144.x: The PM's High Level Committee on the status of Muslims (2005, report 2006) was chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar.

144.s: As per the recommendations of the Sachar Committee, which among the following Muslim groups needs additional attention, similar to that of Hindu OBCs?
144.x: Sachar placed the Ajlaf (backward Muslim converts) as needing attention like Hindu OBCs. The Arzal (Dalit Muslims) compare with SCs, and the Ashraf are the upper group.

144.s: The Rangnath Mishra Commission report which was tabled in the Parliament in December 2009, relates to –
144.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission was the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities (2004); its 2007 report was tabled in December 2009.

144.s:
Match List I (Committee) with List II (Key fact):
List I (Committee)
a. Gopal Singh Committee
b. Ranganath Misra Commission
c. Sachar Committee
d. Kundu Committee
List II (Key fact)
1. Post-Sachar evaluation; Diversity Index and anti-discrimination law
2. Reported on minority welfare in 1983
3. Social, economic and educational status of Muslims (report 2006)
4. 15% reservation for minorities, 10% for Muslims
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: Gopal Singh = 1983 report; Ranganath Misra = 15% (10% Muslims) and delinking SC status from religion; Sachar = status of Muslims, report Nov 2006; Kundu = post-Sachar evaluation 2013-14.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sachar Committee:
1. It was set up in March 2005 and submitted its report in November 2006.
2. It found Muslims under-represented in public employment and higher education.
3. It proposed a National Linguistic Minorities Commission.
4. It described the Arzal as the most deprived group of Muslims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sachar proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority, not a National Linguistic Minorities Commission.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Communal Award was announced in 1932.
2. The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 under Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was set up in 1996.
4. The Kundu Committee recommended a Diversity Index and an Equal Opportunity Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the National Foundation for Communal Harmony dates from 1992.

144.s: The Roshini Scheme implemented by Andhra Pradesh is aimed at providing?
o: Self Employment, Skill development and scholarships to Minority Students
Self Employment, Skill development and scholarships to Muslim Students only
Self Employment, Skill development and scholarships to Christian Students only
A scheme for providing only post matric scholarships to minorities
144.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
144.x: Roshini (AP State Minorities Finance Corporation) gives self-employment, skill development and scholarship support to minority students of all minorities, not only Muslims or Christians.

144.s: The State in India which made Urdu as the second official language is
144.x: Andhra Pradesh made Urdu its second official language in specified districts under Sec. 7 of the AP Official Language Act 1966, extended to all districts in 2022. In J&K Urdu was the official language, not the second.

144.s: In the "Tatkal" scheme implemented by Andhra Pradesh state Minorities Finance Corporation (APSMFC), upto how much amount of loan can a beneficiary get?
144.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
144.x: APSMFC's Tatkal scheme gave small loans of up to Rs 20,000 (as keyed).

144.s:
Consider the following statements about minority welfare in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a statutory State Minorities Commission.
2. The Dulhan scheme gives Rs 1 lakh to minority brides.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: AP has a statutory State Minorities Commission; Dulhan gives Rs 50,000, while Rs 1 lakh is under Shaadi Tohfa.

144.s: What monthly honorarium does Andhra Pradesh pay muezzins?
144.x: Andhra Pradesh pays Rs 10,000 a month to imams and Rs 5,000 a month to muezzins.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about minority welfare in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Urdu was first made a second official language under Section 7 of the AP Official Language Act, 1966, in specified districts.
2. The AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022 extended Urdu to all districts.
3. Shaadi Tohfa (2020) gives Rs 50,000 to minority brides.
4. Imams are paid an honorarium of Rs 10,000 a month.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Shaadi Tohfa gives Rs 1 lakh; Rs 50,000 was the Dulhan scheme (2015).

144.s: Who was the chief Architect of Devathaas?
144.x: In Hindu tradition Vishwakarma is the divine architect of the gods (devatas). Maya was the architect of the asuras.

144.s:
Identify the incorrect statement regarding 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme:

I. The Government of India launched the 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme to provide end-to-end support to fishermen with non-mechanized boats.

II. 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme provides collateral free enterprise development loan up to Rs. 6 lakhs in two tranches.
144.x: Both are incorrect: PM Vishwakarma supports artisans in 18 trades (not fishermen), and its collateral-free loan is up to Rs 3 lakh (1 + 2 lakh) in two tranches, not Rs 6 lakh.

144.s: For whom is the NBCFDC's New Swarnima scheme meant?
144.x: New Swarnima is for women and Saksham for young professionals; Virasat loans for artisans are associated with NMDFC.
xa: NBCFDC (**1992**, MoSJE) lends through **State Channelising Agencies**.
NMDFC also gives **education loans** and **micro-finance**.

144.s: What was the main reason cited for the low expenditure under the SEED scheme?
o: States did not issue DNT certificates
the scheme covered only urban areas
the Union Government withdrew the scheme
beneficiaries were excluded from health insurance
144.x: Low expenditure was attributed to the failure of States to issue certificates for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Link the implementation shortfall to the administrative bottleneck rather than to the scheme’s objectives.
xs: SEED was under-spent because **States did not issue DNT certificates** — option **(1)**.
Only **Rs 69.3 crore** of **Rs 200 crore** was spent in five years.
xa: A special **DNT policy** was demanded in **Vijayawada**.
**Census 2027** will count DNTs.

144.s: Through which agencies do NBCFDC and NMDFC lend to beneficiaries?
144.x: Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through State Channelising Agencies.

144.s: For whom is the NBCFDC's Saksham scheme meant?
144.x: NBCFDC's Saksham is for young professionals; New Swarnima is for women.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Vishwakarma:
1. It covers artisans and craftspeople in 18 trades.
2. It offers collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 2 lakh at 5% interest.
3. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the Ministry of MSME.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM-YASASVI covers OBC, EBC and DNT students with family income below Rs 2.5 lakh.
2. 33% of PM-YASASVI slots are earmarked for girls.
3. SHREYAS supports SC students in higher education such as IITs and IIMs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 30% of PM-YASASVI slots are for girls.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about Denotified Tribes (DNTs):
1. The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 was repealed in 1952.
2. The Idate Commission was the first commission on DNTs.
3. The SEED scheme (2022) has an outlay of Rs 200 crore and its portal is run by the Department of Social Justice.
4. DNTs are to be counted in Census 2027.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Three are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Renke Commission (2008) was the first on DNTs; the Idate Commission found 267-268 DNTs never classified.

144.s:
Match List I (Finance corporation) with List II (Target group):
List I (Body)
a. NSFDC (1989)
b. NBCFDC (1992)
c. NSTFDC (2001)
d. NMDFC
List II (For)
1. Minorities (Virasat loans for artisans)
2. Scheduled Tribes
3. Scheduled Castes
4. Backward Classes
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: NSFDC = SCs (1989); NBCFDC = BCs (1992, MoSJE); NSTFDC = STs (2001); NMDFC = minorities under MoMA.

144.s: As far as possible, how much portion of funds under PMAY (G) at National level are to earmarked for Minorities?
144.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
144.x: PMAY-G earmarks 15% of funds at the national level for minorities (60% for SC/ST), in line with the 15-point programme.

144.s: Which of the following statements about Naya Savera & Nai Udaan is incorrect?
o: It is meant for students clearing UPSC and SSC Main examinations.
It provides financial support to minority students.
It provides free coaching to minority students.
It is associated with the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
144.x: Option A is incorrect: Naya Savera and Nai Udaan support minority students who clear the UPSC or SSC prelims, not the mains.
n: The nodal ministry for Naya Savera and Nai Udaan is the Ministry of Minority Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Minorities are a target group of welfare mechanisms. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Nai Udaan is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the schemes are for students clearing **UPSC and SSC Main** — option **(1)**; they support those clearing the **prelims**.
**Naya Savera** and **Nai Udaan** give **free coaching** and **financial support** to **minority students** under **Minority Affairs**.
xa: ⚠ **Nai Roshni** = women's leadership; **Nai Manzil** = dropouts; **Nai Udaan** = after prelims; **Naya Savera** = coaching.
**Seekho aur Kamao** (**2014**): skilling linked to jobs.

144.s: What is the full form of PM VIKAS, a Central Sector scheme of 2022 merging five minority schemes?
o: Pradhan Mantri Vikas Aur Kaushal Samvardhan
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Aur Kala Sanrakshan
144.x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan; it merges five schemes and runs until 2025-26.
xa: Merged: **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
About **9 lakh** beneficiaries; **33%** of skilling seats for women; linked to **NMDFC** loans.

144.s: Up to what family income are post-matric scholarships given to minority students?
144.x: The minority post-matric scholarship has an income ceiling of Rs 2 lakh, paid by DBT through the National Scholarship Portal.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister's 15 Point Programme for minorities:
1. The original 15-Point Programme was introduced in 1983 and the New 15 Point Programme in 2006.
2. About 15% of targets and outlays in selected schemes are earmarked for minorities.
3. Delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion is one of its aims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: delinking SC status from religion was a Ranganath Misra recommendation; the programme's aims are education, fair share in jobs, living conditions and prevention of communal riots.

144.s:
Match List I (Scheme of the Ministry of Minority Affairs) with List II (Focus):
List I (Scheme)
a. Nai Roshni
b. Seekho aur Kamao
c. Nai Manzil
d. USTTAD
List II (Focus)
1. Education plus skills for school dropouts
2. Leadership training for minority women
3. Traditional arts and crafts
4. Modern skilling with placement
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: Nai Roshni (2013) = leadership for minority women; Seekho aur Kamao (2014) = modern skilling with placement; Nai Manzil (2015) = education + skills for dropouts; USTTAD (2015) = traditional arts and crafts.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM VIKAS is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2022.
2. PM VIKAS merges five schemes, including the PM Jan Vikas Karyakram.
3. 33% of the skilling seats under PM VIKAS are reserved for women.
4. PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured in 2018 from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Two (3 and 4) are correct. PM VIKAS is a Central Sector scheme (1 wrong), and it merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil, not PMJVK (2 wrong); PMJVK is Centrally Sponsored.

144.s: What was the key focus of the Waqf Amendment Bill introduced in April, 2025 ?
o: Enhancing transparency and ensuring better governance
144.x: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill (introduced 8 August 2024, passed April 2025) aimed at transparency, accountability and better governance of waqf properties.

144.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Waqf Act, 1954
B. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2013
C. Waqf Act, 1995
D. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
144.x: The correct sequence is Waqf Act 1954, Waqf Act 1995, Waqf (Amendment) Act 2013, and Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025.
144.tq: Place the parent enactments before their later amendments.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)**.
**Waqf Act 1954** → **Waqf Act 1995** (current parent law) → **Wakf (Amendment) Act 2013** → **2025** changes.
xa: The **Central Waqf Council** became statutory in **1964**.
UMEED portal launched **June 2025**.

144.s: The Waqf Act, 1995 primarily deals with which of the following?
144.x: The Waqf Act, 1995, governs the administration of waqf properties. Tribal forest rights fall under the Forest Rights Act, and free legal aid under the Legal Services Authorities Act.
144.tq: Match each Act to its purpose.
xs: The **Waqf Act, 1995** is the parent law for the **administration of Waqf properties** — option **(4)**.
It replaced the **Waqf Act 1954**.
xa: The **Central Waqf Council** (statutory, **1964**) now sits under **Sec. 9** of the 1995 Act.
The **2013** amendment bars sale, gift or mortgage of waqf property.
All waqf properties go on a **central portal within 6 months** (**UMEED**, June **2025**).

144.s: What is the name of the central portal launched in June 2025 for waqf properties?
144.x: Under the 2025 Act all waqf properties go on a central portal, the UMEED portal (June 2025).

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. It renamed the Waqf Act, 1995 as the UMEED Act.
2. Each State Waqf Board must have at least two non-Muslim members.
3. An appeal lies to the High Court within 60 days.
4. All waqf properties were to be placed on a central portal within six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the appeal to the High Court lies within 90 days.

144.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court's interim order of September 2025 capped non-Muslim members of a State Waqf Board at three.
Reason (R): The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 requires at least two non-Muslim members on each Board.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora.
Only services provided in government hospitals are covered by consumer law.
146.x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.
146.tq: Use the paid-versus-wholly-free distinction to identify the holding.
xs: **IMA v. V.P. Shantha (1995):** **paid medical services**, including those in hospitals charging some patients, are a **"service"** under the Consumer Protection Act — option **(2)**.
So **medical negligence** can go to consumer fora; only **wholly free** services are excluded.
xa: A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.
CPA 2019 brought **product liability** of service providers.

146.s:

146.x: 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: mediation cells are attached to the District, State and National Commissions, not High Courts.

146.s:

146.x: 1 and 3 are correct. Admissibility is decided within 21 days (2 wrong), and a buyer for resale or commercial purpose is excluded from 'consumer' (4 wrong).

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

146.s: In which year was the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission set up?

xa: District → State appeal: **45 days**; State → National: **30 days**.

147.s: Which one of the following is NOT a principle of "Panchsheel"?
o: Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs
147.x: Panchsheel's five principles are territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence; non-alignment is a separate policy, not one of them.

o: Mutual respect for each other’s territorial integrity
Mutual non-interference in each other’s internal affairs

o: Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs
Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
147.x: Panchsheel's five principles are territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence; non-alignment is a separate policy, not one of them.

II. Mutual protection of the environment.

III. Mutual protection of indigenous population.

IV. Mutual non-aggression.

147.x: Peaceful co-existence (I) and mutual non-aggression (IV) are Panchsheel principles; protection of the environment or of indigenous populations is not, so the answer is I and IV.

147.s: We, along with China, are celebrating 50 years of Panchsheel. Apart from us, which country was associated in proposing Panchsheel?

147.s:

4. In 1957 the UN General Assembly took up India's resolution on peaceful co-existence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
147.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Burma adopted it in June 1954 (Zhou Enlai-U Nu joint statement), before Bandung (April 1955).

151.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
151.x: In 2019 Sri Lanka waived the tourist visa fee for citizens of 48 countries, including India, to promote tourism.

151.s: ……… is the largest city in Sri Lanka.
151.x: Colombo is Sri Lanka's largest city and commercial capital (Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital).

151.s: The islands of ______ and ______ are the nearest neighbouring countries that are located in the Indian Ocean.
151.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer & Royalty Inspector Gen
151.x: Sri Lanka and the Maldives are India's nearest island neighbours in the Indian Ocean; Mauritius and Seychelles are farther away, and Indonesia/Malaysia are maritime neighbours but not island nations near the Indian peninsula in the same sense.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987:
1. It was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene.
2. It provided for the merger of the Northern and Western provinces.
3. It provided for provincial councils through the 13th Amendment of Sri Lanka's Constitution.
4. The IPKF sent under it was withdrawn on the order of Rajiv Gandhi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
151.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the merger was of the Northern and Eastern provinces. 4 is wrong: the IPKF (Operation Pawan) was withdrawn on V.P. Singh's order; the last troops left on 24 March 1990.

151.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Katchatheevu was ceded by India to Sri Lanka in 1976.
2. India banned the LTTE in 1992, after the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi.
3. In 2009 the Sri Lankan Army crushed the LTTE and its chief V. Prabhakaran was killed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Katchatheevu was ceded in 1974.

151.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The India-funded Kankesanthurai (KKS) port upgrade is in Sri Lanka.
2. Hambantota port is seen as part of Pakistan's encirclement of India.
3. India gave Sri Lanka economic crisis support of about $4 billion in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Hambantota is part of Chinese, not Pakistani, encirclement.

151.s: Who was elected as the Prime Minister of Nepal for third time?
151.x:
Oli later had a fourth term (July 2024–September 2025) — now Balen Shah (RSP) is Nepal's PM since March 2026 (Praveen CA-360 March 2026)
K.P. Sharma Oli became Nepal's PM for the third time in 2021 (after 2015 and 2018 terms); Deuba had more terms, Bhandari was President. (Now: Oli had a fourth term 2024–Sept 2025; Balen Shah became PM in March 2026.)

151.s: Nepal's first elected President is
151.x: Dr. Ram Baran Yadav became Nepal's first President in July 2008; Paramananda Jha was the first Vice-President.

151.s: Nepal's first elected President is
151.x: Ram Baran Yadav was elected the first President of Nepal in July 2008.

151.s: Who is the first Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal?
151.x: Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' became the first PM of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal in August 2008; Ram Baran Yadav was the first President.

151.s: The first Prime Minister of the Republic of Nepal was :
151.x: Prachanda (UCPN-Maoist) became the first PM of republican Nepal in August 2008.

151.s: According to 2022 Report of U.S. Department of State on International Religious Freedom, which of these religions has the highest population in Nepal (as per Census 2011)?
151.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
151.x: Nepal is a Hindu-majority country: Hinduism had about 81% of the population in the 2011 Census (the figure the US State Department report cites), far ahead of Buddhism (about 9%), Islam and Christianity.

151.s: Which treaty is associated with an open border and security cooperation, while Nepal seeks its revision?
o: India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950
151.x: The 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship provides for an open border and security cooperation; Nepal has sought its revision.
151.tq: Match the treaty's distinctive features with its correct bilateral relationship.
xs: The **India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950** provides an **open border** and **security cooperation**; **Nepal wants it revised** — option **(3)**.
The **Bhutan treaty** is **1949**; the **Land Boundary Agreement** (**1974**) exchanged enclaves; the **Ganga Water Treaty** (**1996**) is on water.
xa: In **2026**, Nepal's **youth-led leadership** is pushing to revise the **1950 Treaty**.
Other Nepal agreements: **Kosi (1954)**, **Gandak (1959)**, **Mahakali (1996)**.

151.s: What is the estimated hydropower potential of Nepal?
151.x: Nepal's hydropower potential is put at 83,000 MW; the first trilateral power deal had Nepal supplying Bangladesh through the Indian grid.
xa: Bhutan projects: **Mangdechhu** (**2019**), **Punatsangchhu I and II**.
Nepal projects: **Pancheshwar**, **Arun III**.

151.s: Under the first trilateral power deal in the region, through which route does Nepal supply electricity to Bangladesh?
151.x: Nepal supplies power to Bangladesh through the Indian grid, the first trilateral power trade.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about Nepal:
1. Nepal's first Constituent Assembly abolished the monarchy on 28 May 2008.
2. Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda', the first PM of the Federal Democratic Republic, belonged to the Nepali Congress.
3. Nepal's new Constitution was adopted on 20 September 2015.
How many of the above statements are correct?
151.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Prachanda belonged to the UCPN (Maoist).

151.s:
Match List-I (India–Nepal treaty) with List-II (Associated with):
List-I | List-II
a. Kosi Agreement | i. Kalapani–Limpiyadhura–Lipulekh dispute (1816)
b. Gandak Agreement | ii. 1954
c. Mahakali Treaty | iii. Pancheshwar project (1996)
d. Sugauli Treaty | iv. 1959
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
151.x: Kosi – 1954; Gandak – 1959; Mahakali Treaty (1996, with Nepal, not Bangladesh) – Sarada, Tanakpur, Pancheshwar; Sugauli Treaty (1816) – base of the Kalapani–Limpiyadhura–Lipulekh dispute (Nepal's new map 2020).

152.s: Which one of the following is not one of the objectives of Act East Policy?
o: To promote economic cooperation cultural ties and develop strategic relationship with countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
To promote peace and amity with the neighbouring countries of Asia.
To place emphasis on India ASEAN cooperation in India’s domestic agenda.
To provide enhanced connectivity to the North East of India.
152.x: MEA lists Act East's objectives as economic cooperation, cultural ties and strategic relationship with the Asia-Pacific, enhanced connectivity to the North-East, and India-ASEAN cooperation in the domestic agenda; 'peace and amity with neighbouring countries of Asia' is not one of them (that is closer to Neighbourhood First).

152.s:
Consider the following statements with regard to India's Foreign Policy:

I. India's Act East Policy was originally conceived as an economic initiative but had later extended into political, strategic and cultural dimensions.

II. The 'Connect Central Asia Policy' has been taken forward with the institutionalization of the 'India-Central Asia Summit' mechanism.

III. Under the 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) Policy, the DRDO initiated the Marine and Allied Interdisciplinary Training and Research Initiative (MAITRI) for the purpose of establishing long-term collaboration with countries in the East Asian region.

IV. India's Think West Policy is an outreach to the Western Industrialized nations for strengthening of relations in areas of education and defence.
Which of the above statements are valid?
152.x: I and II are valid: Act East grew from an economic to a political, strategic and cultural policy, and Connect Central Asia was institutionalised through the India-Central Asia Summit (2022). III is wrong – MAITRI is DRDO's research arm of Sagar Maitri for Indian Ocean Region countries, not East Asia; IV is wrong – Think West is about West Asia (Gulf, Iran, Israel), not Western industrialised nations.

152.s: IMBEX is a joint exercise conducted regularly between Armies of India and
152.x: IMBEX (India-Myanmar Bilateral Exercise) is the regular army exercise between India and Myanmar.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the India’s Look East Policy.

I. It was articulated during the reign of HD Deve Gowda as India’s Prime Minister.

II. It is directed towards South Asian Region.

III. It is about controlling terrorism.

IV. It seeks to develop a bond among various countries on the basis of economic cooperation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
152.x:
The printed stem says 'South Asian Region'; Look East was directed at South-East Asia, so strictly only IV is correct. The key 'II and IV' reads statement II as South-East Asia, as in the original NDA 2010 paper.
Statement I is wrong – Look East was articulated under P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991-92), not Deve Gowda; III is wrong – it was an economic, not a counter-terrorism, policy; IV is right. II is right only as the original question reads it – 'directed towards the South-East Asian region'; the stem's 'South Asian' is a misprint, since Look East never targeted South Asia.

152.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about East Asia Summit?

a. 13th East Asia Summit was held in Singapore

b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum

c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN member

d. East Asia Summit comprises of the ten member states of the ASEAN
152.src: APPSC AEE Civil & Mechanical Engineering General Studies & M
152.x: a, b and c are correct: the 13th EAS was held in Singapore (Nov 2018), the EAS is ASEAN-centred and only an ASEAN member chairs it. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members (10 ASEAN + 8 partners incl. India, China, USA, Russia).

a. 13th East Asia Summit held in Singapore.

b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum.

c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN Member.

d. East Asia Summit comprises the ten member states of the ASEAN.
152.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
152.x: a, b and c are correct: 13th EAS in Singapore (2018), ASEAN-centred, chaired only by an ASEAN member. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members, not just the ten ASEAN states; so 'all of the above' is wrong.

152.s: The second edition of India Myanmar Naval Exercise IMNEX-2019 was organised at:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: IMNEX-2019, the second India-Myanmar Naval Exercise, was held at Visakhapatnam (19-22 October 2019), like the first edition in 2018.

152.s:
Match List-I (Policy) with List-II (Associated with):
List-I | List-II
a. Look East | i. SAARC leaders at the PM's swearing-in, May 2014
b. Act East | ii. P.V. Narasimha Rao, 1991–92
c. Neighbourhood First | iii. East Asia Summit in Myanmar, 2014
d. Link West | iv. Gulf, Iran and Israel
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
152.x: Look East – Narasimha Rao, 1991–92 (economic, ASEAN); Act East – launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar, 2014 (not a SAARC Summit); Neighbourhood First – May 2014 swearing-in with SAARC leaders; Link West/Think West – West Asia: Gulf, Iran, Israel.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Countering China, new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were drivers of the Look East Policy.
2. Climate action is the fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of Act East.
3. Under Act East, India's North-East is treated as the gateway to ASEAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the fourth C is Capacity building, not Climate action.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Act East:
1. The Akhaura–Agartala rail link is an ASEAN-linked connectivity project with Myanmar.
2. India and Vietnam raised their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.
3. The Philippines became India's strategic partner in August 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Akhaura–Agartala is a rail link with Bangladesh, not ASEAN; the ASEAN-linked projects are Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway.

152.s: Dustlik-2019 - a first ever joint military exercise was held between India and ___:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: DUSTLIK is the India-Uzbekistan joint military exercise; its first edition was held in November 2019 at Tashkent.

152.s: What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
o: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
152.x: Chabahar gives India an alternative route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, which denies India land transit.

152.s: Through which port of Iran, India sent its consignment of wheat in October, 2017 to Afghanistan by passing the Pakistan route?
152.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
152.x: India's first wheat shipment to Afghanistan (October 2017) went through Iran's Chabahar port, bypassing Pakistan.

152.s: What bilateral trade target was set when India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026?
152.x: The August 2026 upgrade set a $5 billion trade target by 2030, along with a uranium-supply framework.
xa: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (**Samarkand, 2019**).
Other upgrades: **Vietnam** CSP **2016**; **Malaysia** CSP **2024**; **Philippines** strategic partner **Aug 2025**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Link West engagement:
1. India's trade with the GCC is over $160 billion.
2. The first I2U2 leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. I2U2 is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: All three are correct: GCC trade exceeds $160 billion, the first I2U2 summit was virtual (2022) and it is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about India and Central Asia:
1. The Connect Central Asia policy was launched in 2012 at Bishkek.
2. The first India-Central Asia Summit of January 2022 was held physically in New Delhi.
3. The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was held at Samarkand in 2019, with Afghanistan invited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the first India-Central Asia Summit (January 2022) was held virtually; it institutionalised the Connect Central Asia policy.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In 2026 the USA extended India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar port.
Reason (R): Chabahar, on the Gulf of Oman, gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia without depending on Pakistan.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
152.x: A is false: in 2026 the USA ended, not extended, the waiver. R is true: Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman, linked to INSTC, and bypasses Pakistan.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad', comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the USA.
2. India's Think West doctrine has widened into the I2U2.
3. The GCC, India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, hosts an Indian diaspora of about 1 million.
How many of the above statements are correct?
152.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the GCC hosts about 10 million Indians (trade over $160 billion).

152.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to Information Fusion Centre (IFC) for the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and choose the correct code given below:
a. It is established with a prime vision to strengthen maritime security in the region and beyond
b. Its prime goal is to create maritime information hub for joint satellite mission in the region
c. It has been established at Gurugram, India and is jointly administered by the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard.
152.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
152.x: a and c are correct: the IFC-IOR at IMAC Gurugram (Dec 2018) aims at maritime security through information sharing, and IMAC is jointly administered by the Indian Navy and the Coast Guard. b is wrong – it is not a hub for a joint satellite mission.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's maritime visions?
o: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region
SAGAR was announced in Sri Lanka in 2015
MAHASAGAR (2025) stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar
152.x: SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025) were both announced in Mauritius, not Sri Lanka.
xa: ⚠ SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were both launched in **Mauritius**; **SHANTI** by **EAM Jaishankar**, not the PM.
SHANTI will be operationalised first in the **Bay of Bengal**.

152.s:
Match List-I (India's maritime vision) with List-II (When announced):
List-I | List-II
a. SAGAR | i. November 2019
b. MAHASAGAR | ii. 2025
c. SHANTI | iii. 2015
d. IPOI | iv. July 2026
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
152.x: SAGAR – 2015, Mauritius; MAHASAGAR – 2025, Mauritius; SHANTI – 13 July 2026, EAM Jaishankar; IPOI – 14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok, November 2019.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the full forms of India's maritime visions:
1. MAHASAGAR stands for Maritime and Holistic Alliance for Security and Growth Across Regions.
2. SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region.
3. SHANTI stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: MAHASAGAR is Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under SAGAR, India projects itself as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.
2. SHANTI is to be operationalised first in the Arabian Sea.
3. The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a trilateral of India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: SHANTI is to be applied first in the Bay of Bengal.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's coastal surveillance radar chain covers Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles.
2. The coastal radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects are flagships of the SAGAR doctrine.
3. MILAN 2026 was held at Kochi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam, tying Andhra Pradesh to Act East and SAGAR.

152.s: Where was the 14th East Asia Summit of November 2019, at which PM Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, held?
152.x: IPOI was proposed at the 14th EAS in Bangkok; it is an open, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars that builds on SAGAR.
xa: Pillars include **Maritime Security**, **Maritime Ecology**, **Maritime Resources**, **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**.
**Spain** joined the IPOI in **Jan 2026**.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
152.x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.
152.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the formally listed seven pillars.
xs: **Nuclear Disarmament Verification** is not an IPOI pillar — option **(4)**.
The **7 pillars**: **Maritime Security**; **Maritime Ecology**; **Maritime Resources**; **Capacity Building and Resource Sharing**.
Also: **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**; **Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation**; **Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport**.
xa: IPOI was proposed at the **14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok** (**Nov 2019**).
IPOI is open, **non-treaty**, and builds on **SAGAR**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM Modi set out India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue in June 2018.
2. The Shangri-La Dialogue is organised by Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
3. The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative has seven pillars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Dialogue, held in Singapore since 2002, is run by the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS).

152.s: In 2019, the leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in, extending Neighbourhood First?
152.x: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014; BIMSTEC leaders in 2019.

2. Assumption Island – Maldives

152.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Assumption Island is in Seychelles. 4 is wrong: Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour is in the Maldives.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Neighbourhood First was marked by the invitation to SAARC leaders to the PM's swearing-in in May 2014.
Reason (R): The Gujral Doctrine, a root of Neighbourhood First, emphasised non-reciprocity towards neighbours.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
152.x: Both are true: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014 (BIMSTEC in 2019), and the Gujral Doctrine stressed non-reciprocity and non-interference. But R is a background principle, not the explanation of the 2014 invitation.

153.s: India participated in a joint military drill called 'Vajra Prahar 2018' in Jaipur on 1st December 2018. Name the country with whom this joint exercise was performed.

o: joint military exercise between India and USA
joint military exercise between India and Japan
joint tiger conservation exercise between India and USA
joint tiger conservation exercise between India and Japan
153.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

153.s: In which area was the Indo-US military exercise 'Yudh Abhyas 2014' held ?
153.x: Yudh Abhyas 2014 was held from 17 to 30 September 2014 at Chaubattia, Ranikhet (Uttarakhand).

o: It is an Indian military exercise with regard to Pakistan.
It is an Indian military exercise with Oman.
It is an Indian military exercise with Bhutan.
It is an Indian military exercise with the US.

153.s: What was the code name given to the first ever tri-service military exercise between India and USA?
153.x: Tiger Triumph is the first India-US tri-service amphibious exercise (2019).

153.s: "Malabar Exercise-2016" is a joint Naval exercise of the following Countries
153.x: Malabar 2016 was a trilateral naval exercise of India, the USA and Japan (Australia rejoined in 2020).

153.s: In which State was the India-US army exercise Yudh Abhyas held in November 2022?
153.x: Yudh Abhyas of November 2022 was held in Uttarakhand.

153.x: Vajra Prahar – Special Forces (2018 edition, Jaipur); Cope India – Air Force; Malabar – Navy, with Japan and Australia; Yudh Abhyas – Army (annual since 2004).

153.x: Leon Panetta, US Secretary of Defense, visited India in June 2012. John Bryson was Commerce Secretary, Eric Holder Attorney General and Hillary Clinton Secretary of State.

153.x: GSOMIA protects shared military information and COMCASA covers encrypted communications; BECA (2020) concerns geospatial data, so statement 2 is wrong.

To strengthen cordial relations between U.S and

153.s:

156.s: Which one of the following cities was named by UNESCO as World Capital of Architecture for 2020?

156.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione

156.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
156.x: In 2019 UNESCO named Mumbai (film) and Hyderabad (gastronomy) Creative Cities among 66 new members.

o: For not recognizing historic sites in USA
For maintaining relations with North Korea
For recognizing Nazi sites in Germany as historic sites
Against anti Israel bias of the Organization

UNESCO Executive Board: **58** members.

156.x: The Bhagavad Gita manuscripts and the Natyashastra are on the Memory of the World register.

156.x: 1 and 3 are correct (194 Member States + 12 Associate Members). 2 is wrong: the Information for All Programme (IFAP) is a UNESCO programme, like Man and the Biosphere.

156.s:

156.s: Which was the first UN organisation to start accepting Cryptocurrency donations?
156.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

156.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
156.x: UNICEF's Cryptocurrency Fund (October 2019) made it the first UN organisation to hold and make transactions in cryptocurrency; UNDP, WHO and FAO did not.

156.s: The International Organization that has launched the "Freedom from Hunger" campaign in 1960 was :
156.x: The FAO launched the 'Freedom from Hunger' campaign in 1960 to mobilise action against world hunger; UNDP, WHO and UNICEF did not.

156.s: Which of the following UN agencies works in for the upliftment of well-being of children?
156.x: UNICEF (UN Children's Fund) is the UN body for children's rights and well-being; the WTO and IMF are economic bodies and UNESCO handles education, science and culture.

156.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
156.x: UNICEF (UN Children's Fund) has the mandate of children's rights and well-being. WTO and IMF are economic bodies, and UNESCO deals with education, science and culture.

156.x: Y.K. Modi was elected to the ILO Governing Body (employers' group) in 2011; the Governing Body is the ILO's tripartite executive body, not part of UNCTAD, the WTO or the WEF.

156.s: At which one of the following place, the World Health Organisation (WHO) is going to establish Global Traditional Medicine Centre?
156.x: The WHO and India signed the agreement for the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in March 2022; it is at Jamnagar, Gujarat – the first such global centre.

156.src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,

156.s: Who among the following Indian actresses received UNICEF's 'Danny Kaye Humanitarian Award' in December 2019?
156.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

156.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M

156.x: WHO (1948) is the directing and coordinating authority for international health work within the UN system and promotes health research.

156.x: UNFPA deals with population and publishes the State of World Population.

156.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and ILO conventions:
1. India has ratified C29 and C105.
2. India has ratified C100 and C111.
3. India has ratified C189 on Domestic Workers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: India has ratified C29, C105, C100 and C111. It has not ratified the Domestic Workers Convention C189, adopted by the ILC in 2011.
156.tq: Use the convention number and ratification status together to identify the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: India has ratified **C29** and **C105** (forced labour).
Statement 2: India has ratified **C100** (equal remuneration) and **C111** (discrimination).
Statement 3 wrong: India has **not ratified C189** on Domestic Workers (adopted **2011**).
xa: India ratified **C138** and **C182** in **2017**.
Also not ratified: **C87** (freedom of association) and **C98** (collective bargaining).
The ILO is the **leading normative agency** on labour standards.

156.s: According to the ILO-UNICEF estimate released in 2025, about how many child labourers were there in 2024?
156.x: Child labour fell from 160 million (2020) to about 138 million (2024, released 2025).

156.s: According to SOFI 2026, to about what level did global hunger fall for the third year?
156.x: SOFI 2026 reported hunger falling for the third year to 7.8% (645 million).

156.s:
Match List-I (Report) with List-II (Agency):
List-I | List-II

b. World Employment and Social Outlook | ii. UNEP
c. Emissions Gap Report | iii. ILO
d. State of World Population | iv. UNFPA

156.x: Human Development Report – UNDP; World Employment and Social Outlook – ILO; Emissions Gap Report – UNEP (not UNESCO); State of World Population – UNFPA.

156.x: WFP – India's five-year rice supply deal (2026); UNDP – Global MPI with OPHI; GEF (1992) – UNDP, UNEP, World Bank; WHO – Global Centre for Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar (agreement with AYUSH, March 2022).

156.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Representatives of employers and workers sit, along with governments, in the ILO's Governing Body.
Reason (R): The ILO has a tripartite structure of governments, employers and workers.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
156.x: Both are true and R explains A: the tripartite structure operates in the International Labour Conference and the Governing Body (Y.K. Modi was elected to it in 2011 from the employers' group).

156.s:
Consider the following statements about India and ILO conventions:

156.x: 1 and 3 are correct (C189, 2011, not ratified by India). 2 is wrong: India ratified C138 and C182 in 2017.

Consider the following statements:

3. The ILO's Employment and Social Trends 2026 puts global unemployment at 4.9 per cent.
4. The Emissions Gap Report 2025 says current policies put the world on course for about 2.8°C.
How many of the above statements are correct?
156.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: SOFI is published jointly by FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO.

156.s: Who was selected for the Nobel Peace Prize, 2020?
156.x: The World Food Programme received the Nobel Peace Prize for 2020 for its efforts to combat hunger and prevent its use as a weapon of war; Wilson and Milgrom won the 2020 economics prize.

156.s: The World Food Day is observed on
156.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie

o: Founding of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)

156.x: World Food Day, 16 October, commemorates the founding of the FAO on 16 October 1945 – not a famine, HYV wheat or Borlaug's birthday.

156.s: 7th December is observed as ____.
156.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
156.x: 7 December is International Civil Aviation Day (ICAO, Chicago Convention 1944); Migrants Day is 18 December, Mountain Day 11 December, Sign Languages Day 23 September.

156.x: International Mother Language Day, proclaimed by UNESCO in 1999, is observed on 21 February; International Yoga Day is on 21 June and International Youth Day on 12 August.

156.x: FAO observes World Soil Day on 5 December. World Health Day (7 April) belongs to WHO, so it is not the answer.

156.x: The United Nations World Refugee Day is observed every year on 20 June.

156.x: UN Peacekeeping Forces won in 1988. The UN with Kofi Annan won in 2001, IPCC with Al Gore in 2007 and UNICEF in 1965.

156.s: In which year did the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) win the Nobel Peace Prize?
156.x: The OPCW won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013.

156.s: In March 2025, India chaired which major UN body in 2025 focused on global drug policy?
o: UN Office on Drugs and Crime

156.s: Name the Indian elected to the International Narcotics Control Board by the UN Economic and Social Council on 23rd April 2014 and re-elected by the Council for a 5-year term (2020-2025) on 7th May, 2019.
156.x: Jagjit Pavadia of India was elected to the International Narcotics Control Board by ECOSOC in 2014 and re-elected in 2019 for 2020-25; Syed Akbaruddin was India's UN envoy.

156.s: As of January 2020, who is the Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Program, who previously held the position of Director General of IUCN?
156.x: Inger Andersen (Denmark), former Director General of IUCN, became UNEP Executive Director in 2019 and still heads UNEP. Grethel Aguilar is the current IUCN Director General.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about India's roles in UN bodies:

2. Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body in 2020-21.

156.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India chaired the 68th session of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, not UNODC.

2. Guy Ryder has been Director-General of the ILO since 2022.
3. India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2025-2028.
How many of the above statements are correct?
156.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Gilbert F. Houngbo has been ILO Director-General since 2022; Guy Ryder was his predecessor.

157.s: When was the International Monetary Fund (IMF) established?
157.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
157.x: The IMF came into formal existence on 27 December 1945, when its Articles of Agreement entered into force with 29 members; it began operations on 1 March 1947.

157.s: How is the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference wherein the agreements were signed to set up IBRD, GATT and IMF, commonly known?
157.x: The UN Monetary and Financial Conference of July 1944 at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire (44 nations) set up the IMF and IBRD – the Bretton Woods twins.

157.s: In the context of international trade, what does abbreviation of IMF means?
157.x: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund; 'International Monetary Funds' is the only option that names it (a misprint of the singular) – 'Form' and 'Monetering' are wrong.

157.s: Regarding the International Monetary Fund, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It can grant loans to any country.
It can grant loans to only developed countries.
It grants loans to only member countries.
It can grant loans to the central bank of a country.
157.x: The IMF provides financial assistance only to its member countries facing balance-of-payments problems.

157.s: The international organization that provided loan assistance to overcome the economic crisis in 1991 is
157.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
157.x: India met the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis with IMF loans (SDR 3.56 billion in 1991), which came with the reform conditions of the New Economic Policy.

157.s: "Rapid Financing Instrument" and "Rapid Credit Facility" are related to the provisions of lending by which one of the following?
o: United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative
157.x: The Rapid Financing Instrument (urgent BoP needs of members) and the Rapid Credit Facility (concessional, for low-income members) are IMF lending facilities.

157.s: How many members did the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have as of January 2020?
157.x:
189 members in January 2020 — now 191 (Nauru 190th in 2021, Liechtenstein 191st on 21 October 2024) (PMF IAS International Relations p.164)
As of January 2020 the IMF had 189 members (now 191, after Nauru in 2021 and Liechtenstein in 2024).

157.s: Which of the following statements is correct with regard to ‘International Monetary Fund’?
o: It can grant loans to country.
It can grant loans to only developed countries.
It grants loans to member countries only.
It grants loans to the Central Bank of a country.
157.x: The IMF lends only to its member countries; project financing is the World Bank's job. So it cannot lend to any country or only to developed ones.

157.s: Recently, which one of the following currencies has been proposed to be added to the basket of the IMF's SDR?
157.x: The IMF decided in 2015 that the Chinese renminbi met the criteria, and it joined the SDR basket on 1 October 2016 – the fifth currency, with the dollar, euro, yen and pound.

157.s: International Monetary Fund was set up in
157.x: The IMF was created at Bretton Woods (1944) and came into existence on 27 December 1945 (operations from 1947). Moved to Bretton Woods institutions.

157.s: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) became operational in the year
157.src: APPSC AP Municipal Junior Accounts Officers 2012
157.x:
APPSC 2012 key and most books: 1945. Strictly the IMF began financial operations on 1 March 1947 (NextGen Part 1 APPSC 02 p.15), so 1947 fits 'became operational' better.
The APPSC 2012 key gives 1945: the IMF came into existence on 27 December 1945, when its Articles of Agreement (Bretton Woods, 1944) took effect.

157.s:
Consider the following statements:

157.x: The PRGF was set up by the IMF (1999), not the IDA, so A is false; the IMF-Singapore Regional Training Institute trains officials in macroeconomic analysis and policy, so B is true.

157.s: International Monetary Fund (IMF) was established in
157.x: The IMF was conceived at Bretton Woods in July 1944 but formally came into existence on 27 December 1945.

157.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economics & Statistical Servi
