157.s: Which one of the following body is not associated to Bretton Woods institutions?
157.x:
The source key reads (b) & (c): neither the UN nor the WTO is a Bretton Woods institution; keyed (b) United Nations as printed.
The Bretton Woods institutions are the IMF and the World Bank. The United Nations is not one of them; the WTO (1995) is not one either, so the stem is loose – the key takes the UN.

157.s: At present, how many countries are the members of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
157.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (191); it is added as option 5.
the key was 190 (2020-24) — now 191 members, Liechtenstein joining in Oct 2024 (imf.org IMF at a Glance)
The printed key 190 held from Andorra's entry in 2020 until 2024 (now 191, Liechtenstein having joined in October 2024), so no printed option is now correct.

157.s: Regarding International Monetary Fund, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It can grant loans to any country
It can grant loans to only developed countries
It grants loans to only member countries
It can grant loans to the Central Bank of a country
157.x: The IMF lends only to its member countries, for balance of payments difficulties; it does not lend to non-members or directly to commercial borrowers.

157.s:
With reference to World Bank and International Monetary Fund, which of the following statements is/ are correct ?
1. The World Bank and International Monetary Fund were set up together and are popularly known as Bretton Wood Twins.
2. Headquarters of International Monetary Fund and World Bank are located at Washington D.C. and New York respectively.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
157.x: The IMF and World Bank were set up together at Bretton Woods and are called the Bretton Woods twins (1 correct); both are headquartered in Washington, D.C., not New York (2 wrong) – so only 1.

157.s: India became a member of International Monetary Fund in :
157.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1945); it is added as option 5.
India is a founding member of the IMF, joining on 27 December 1945 when the Fund came into existence; 1947 is when the IMF began financial operations (1 March 1947), and 1950-52 are wrong.

157.s:
With reference to the International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC), consider the following statements:

A. IMFC discusses matters of concern affecting the global economy, and advises the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on the direction of its work.

B. The World Bank participates as observer in IMFC's meetings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
157.x: Both are correct: the IMFC advises and reports to the IMF Board of Governors and gives strategic direction to the Fund's work, and a number of institutions, including the World Bank, participate as observers in its meetings.

157.s: During India's balance-of-payments crisis in 1991, approximately how much was obtained from the IMF and World Bank, contributing to the New Economic Policy?
157.x: India obtained about $7 billion from the IMF and World Bank during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, preceding the New Economic Policy.
157.tq: Distinguish the billion-scale figure from misleading million and larger-billion alternatives.
xs: India obtained about **$7 billion** from the IMF/World Bank in the **1991 BoP crisis** — option **(1)**.
This led into the **New Economic Policy**.
xa: India's allocated **SDRs** are usable for **BoP** needs.
IBRD's **$1.5 billion** facility supports the **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.
**Criticism**: IMF/WB loans carry **structural adjustment conditions**.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bretton Woods Conference:
1. It was held in July 1944 at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, and was attended by 44 allied nations.
2. Of the two plans before it, that of John Maynard Keynes of the UK was adopted.
3. The International Trade Organization planned there was never created, and GATT (1947) filled the gap until the WTO (1995).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
157.x: 1 and 3 are correct (July 1944, Mount Washington Hotel, Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, 44 allied nations; ITO never born, GATT 1947 until WTO 1995). 2 is wrong: the plan of Harry Dexter White (US) was adopted, not Keynes's.

157.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Smithsonian Agreement of 1971 widened the band of exchange-rate fluctuation to 2.25%.
2. The Smithsonian Agreement lasted about 14 years.
3. The IMF began its financial operations on 1 March 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
157.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Smithsonian Agreement lasted only about 14 months, not 14 years. The IMF began operations on 1 March 1947.

157.s:
Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Date):
List-I | List-II

b. IMF Articles in force – formal existence | ii. July 1944
c. First IMF borrower (France) | iii. 27 December 1945

157.x: Bretton Woods conference – July 1944; IMF formal existence with 29 members – 27 December 1945; France borrowed first on 8 May 1947; SDR created 1967-69, first allocation 1970.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about IMF quotas:
1. Quotas decide a member's financial contribution, its access to borrowing and its voting power.
2. Quotas fix the exchange rate of a member's currency.
3. In the quota formula, GDP carries a weight of 50% and openness 30%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
157.x: 1 and 3 are correct (formula: GDP 50%, openness 30%, variability 15%, reserves 5%). 2 is wrong: quotas do not fix exchange rates.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about IMF membership:
1. India is the 8th largest member by IMF quota, with about 2.75%.
2. Liechtenstein became the 191st member of the IMF in October 2024.
3. Nauru became the 189th member of the IMF in 2021.
How many of the above statements are correct?
157.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Nauru became the 190th member in 2021; the IMF already had 189 members in January 2020.

157.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The United States alone can block major decisions of the IMF.
Reason (R): Major IMF decisions need 85% of the votes and the US holds about 16.5% of them.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
157.x: Both are true and R explains A: with 85% needed and the US holding ~16.5%, the US alone holds a veto.

157.s:

158.tq: Detect the agreement-subject swap among neighbouring WTO agreements.
xs: **GATS — prohibited, actionable and non-actionable subsidies** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**.

158.x: Both the e-commerce moratorium and the TRIPS non-violation moratorium lapsed at MC14; no permanent solution on public stockholding was reached.

158.s:
Match List-I (WTO agreement) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. GATS | i. Trade in services
b. TRIMS | ii. Trade-distorting investment measures such as local content
c. SPS | iii. Technical regulations, standards and conformity assessment
d. TBT | iv. Food safety, animal and plant health
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
158.x: GATS – services; TRIMS – investment measures (local content); SPS – food safety, animal and plant health; TBT – technical regulations and standards.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Phytosanitary rules and technical standards are non-tariff barriers.
2. The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are the only new WTO agreements of its first 30 years.
3. In India, anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard inquiries are conducted by the DGFT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: these trade-remedy inquiries are conducted by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR).

158.s:
Consider the following statements about India and TRIPS:
1. India enacted the Geographical Indications Act in 1999 to meet TRIPS.
2. India amended its Patents Act to allow product patents in 1999.
3. India's first compulsory licence was granted in 2012 in the Natco-Bayer case.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Patents Act was amended for product patents in 2005.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Doha Declaration (2001) affirmed that TRIPS must not stop members from protecting public health.
2. The COVID-19 TRIPS waiver of 2020 was proposed by India and Brazil.
3. MC12 (2022) agreed a limited TRIPS waiver for COVID-19 vaccine patents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the waiver was proposed by India and South Africa, not Brazil.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Section 3(d) of India's Patents Act is one of India's TRIPS flexibilities.
Reason (R): Section 3(d) is meant to promote the evergreening of patents.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
158.x: A is true. R is false: Section 3(d) is an anti-evergreening provision – it blocks evergreening, used with compulsory licensing as India's TRIPS flexibilities.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Amber Box support is trade-distorting and capped.
2. Blue Box support is Amber Box support with production limits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: Both are correct: Amber Box covers trade-distorting support such as price support and is capped; Blue Box is Amber support with production limits.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Green Box support has no limit.
2. The de minimis limit is 10% of production for developing countries and 5% for developed ones.
3. The Peace Clause shielding public stockholding was agreed at Nairobi in 2015.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Peace Clause was agreed at Bali in 2013 (extended by a 2014 decision).

158.s:
Match List-I (WTO dispute against India) with List-II (Year of panel ruling against India):
List-I | List-II
a. Solar panels (JNNSM domestic content) | i. 2016
b. Export subsidies (MEIS, SEZ) | ii. 2019
c. Sugar subsidies | iii. 2023
d. ICT tariffs | iv. 2021
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
158.x: Solar panels – India lost, 2016 (complainant USA); export subsidies – 2019 (USA); sugar subsidies – December 2021 (Brazil, Australia, Guatemala); ICT tariffs – April 2023 (EU, Japan, Chinese Taipei).

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The WTO Appellate Body crisis since 2019 arises from the USA blocking appointments.
2. The dispute over India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ) was brought by the European Union.
3. The dispute over India's solar-panel domestic-content rules was brought by the USA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the MEIS/SEZ export-subsidy case was brought by the USA, not the EU.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, in force since 1998, lapsed on 31 March 2026.
2. Phase 2 of the fisheries subsidies talks, on overcapacity and overfishing, was unresolved at MC14.
3. India supports bringing the Investment Facilitation for Development into the WTO rulebook.
4. The US wants to deny Special and Differential Treatment to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia.
How many of the above statements are correct?
158.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: India opposes the Investment Facilitation for Development.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India's core food-security demand at the WTO is a permanent solution for public stockholding.
Reason (R): The Bali Peace Clause shields developing-country public stockholding only until a permanent solution is found.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
158.x: Both are true and R explains A: the Peace Clause (Bali 2013, extended 2014) is only an interim shield, so India seeks a permanent PSH solution.

158.s: About how many countries took part in the Uruguay Round of trade negotiations?
158.x: The Uruguay Round (1986-93/94) had 123 countries and led to the WTO.

158.s:
Match List-I (Trade round) with List-II (Outcome):
List-I | List-II
a. Kennedy Round (1964-67) | i. Stalled
b. Tokyo Round (1973-79) | ii. First Anti-Dumping Code
c. Uruguay Round (1986-94) | iii. Non-tariff barrier codes
d. Doha Development Agenda (2001) | iv. Created the WTO, TRIPS, GATS and AoA
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
158.x: Kennedy – tariff cuts and first Anti-Dumping Code; Tokyo – NTB codes; Uruguay – WTO, TRIPS, GATS, AoA; Doha – stalled.

159.s: Who authored the Preamble of the proposed Constitution of the European Union?
159.x: Valery Giscard d'Estaing, chairman of the European Convention (2002-03), drafted the preamble of the proposed EU Constitution; Chirac was French President, Druon a writer.

159.s: Why was Roberta Metsola in the news in January 2022?
o: She was elected as the president of the World Bank.
She was elected as the president of the INTERPOL.
She was elected as the president of the European Parliament.
She was elected as the president of UNICEF.
159.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
159.x: Roberta Metsola (Malta) was elected President of the European Parliament in January 2022 - not of the World Bank, INTERPOL or UNICEF.

159.s: How many member states are associated with the organisation of Council of Europe?
159.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
159.x:
Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe in March 2022 — now 46 member states (app notes 2:159 sub 0)
The Council of Europe had 47 member states until Russia was expelled in March 2022 (now 46); 27 is the EU's figure, not the Council of Europe's.

159.s: Which international organisation aims to uphold human rights in Europe?
o: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
159.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
159.x: The Council of Europe (Strasbourg, 1949) upholds human rights, democracy and the rule of law in Europe through the European Convention on Human Rights; OECD and IMF are economic bodies.

159.s: The European Union leaders granted Ukraine and ___ candidate status for EU membership during a European Council meeting in Brussels on June 23, 2022.
159.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
159.x: On 23 June 2022 the European Council granted candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova; Cyprus and Bulgaria are already EU members and Brazil is not European.

159.s: Which Article of European Union Treaty is invoked by Britain as part of Brexit?
159.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
159.x: Britain invoked Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union (the Lisbon Treaty exit clause) for Brexit.

159.s: The Windsor Framework which is formed in February 2023, is associated with which of the following?
o: Northern Ireland, United Kingdom, and the European Union
159.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
159.x: The Windsor Framework (February 2023) is the UK-EU arrangement on trade for Northern Ireland.

159.s: The term 'Digital Single Market Strategy' seen in the news refers to
159.x: The Digital Single Market Strategy is an EU initiative adopted on 6 May 2015.

159.s: Which of the following countries has taken membership of the European Union in July, 2013?
159.x: Croatia joined the EU on 1 July 2013 as its 28th member.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the European Union.

I. The European Union was known earlier as the European Community.

II. The Single European Act (1986) and the Maastricht Treaty were milestones in its formation.

III. Citizens of European Union countries enjoy dual citizenship.

IV. Switzerland is a member of the European Union.
Which of the above statements are correct?
159.x: The EU grew out of the European Community, and the Single European Act (1986) and Maastricht Treaty were milestones; EU citizens hold EU citizenship over and above national citizenship (the 'dual citizenship' of the key); Switzerland is not a member - so I, II and III.

159.s: The basis of European Unions league with the signing of
159.x: The European Union was founded by the Maastricht Treaty (signed 1992, in force 1993); the Treaty of Rome (1957) created only the EEC and the Treaty of Paris (1951) the ECSC.

159.s: BREXIT refers to the Great Britain leaving which one of the following?
159.x: Brexit is the UK's exit from the European Union, under Article 50 TEU, completed on 31 January 2020.

159.s:
Which among the following statements about European Union (EU) are correct ?

I. The EU is the world’s largest economy.

II. The EU has its own flag, anthem and currency.

III. The EU’s combined armed forces are the second largest in the world.

IV. The EU has its own Constitution.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
159.x: NCERT describes the EU as having its own flag, anthem and currency, combined armed forces second largest in the world and (then) the biggest economy alongside the US, but it failed to get its own Constitution - so IV is wrong and I, II, III is the key.

159.s: After Brexit referendum results, the following did not happen in UK:
o: There was a change of Prime Minister
The opposition party came to power
The new Prime Minister is a lady
The Home Secretary became the new Conservative leader
159.x: After the 2016 referendum Cameron resigned and Theresa May, the Home Secretary, became Conservative leader and PM; the Conservatives stayed in power, so the opposition did not come to power.

159.s: The referendum in Greece in June, 2015 was to decide on whether
o: To curtail powers of the Parliament or not
To accept bail out conditions by EU and IMF or not
159.x: The Greek referendum of 5 July 2015 (called in June) asked whether to accept the bailout conditions of the EU, ECB and IMF creditors; it was not about leaving the EU.

159.s: The number of member countries of the European Union is
159.x: The EU had 27 members from January 2007 (Bulgaria, Romania); it became 28 with Croatia (2013) and is 27 again since Brexit (2020).

159.s: Which one of the following is not true for ‘Euro’ in 1999 :
o: It is an unit of account
It is means of deferred payments
It is a mode of payment
159.x: In 1999 the euro existed only as a unit of account (book money); notes and coins went into circulation on 1 January 2002, so 'it is in circulation' was not true.

159.s: On which date did the United Kingdom leave the European Union?
159.x: Using Article 50 TEU, the UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, bringing the EU back to 27.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the European Union:
1. The Treaty of Rome (1957) set up the European Economic Community, the forerunner of the EU.
2. The Maastricht Treaty (1992) created the European Union.
3. Croatia, the latest member, joined the EU in 2007.
4. Brexit was carried out under Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union.
How many of the above statements are correct?
159.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Croatia joined on 1 July 2013; 2007 is when Bulgaria and Romania joined.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Europe:
1. It was founded in 1949 and is headquartered at Strasbourg.
2. It is a body of the European Union.
3. After Russia's expulsion in March 2022 it has 46 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Council of Europe (human rights, democracy, rule of law) is not an EU body.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'Digital Single Market Strategy' is an initiative of ASEAN.
2. Under the India-EU FTA (2026), the EU made commitments in 144 services subsectors.
3. The EU's Stability and Growth Pact limits budget deficits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Digital Single Market Strategy was adopted by the EU on 6 May 2015.

159.s:
The venue for the ASEAN Mekong Basin Commonwealth Bank ODI tri series in cricket Development Cooperation Meeting in August 2007 against Australia by: was:

C) 8 runs
D) 9 runs
o: New Delhi ONGC's supply ship that drowned in the
159.x: The 9th ASEAN-Mekong Basin Development Cooperation (AMBDC) Ministerial Meeting was held in Manila, Philippines, in August 2007 (the printed question is garbled with other items).

159.s: Which one of the following is not an ASEAN member?
159.x: China is not an ASEAN member, only a dialogue partner; Cambodia, Laos and the Philippines are members.

159.s:
India is a member of which among the following?

I. Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation

II. Association of South-East Asian Nations

III. East Asia Summit
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

159.s: Which of following country is not a member of ASEAN?
159.x: South Korea is a dialogue/EAS/RCEP partner of ASEAN, not a member; Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia are members.

159.s: Which of the following countries is not a member of ASEAN?
159.x: India is only a dialogue partner of ASEAN, not a member; Brunei, Cambodia and Vietnam are members.

159.s: In which City, the ASEAN Summit was held recently?
159.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
159.x: The ASEAN Summit of that period (31st Summit, November 2017) was held in Manila under the Philippines' chairmanship.

159.s: The term 'Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership' often appears in the news in the context of the affairs of a group of countries known as
159.x: RCEP is an ASEAN-led free trade agreement of the 10 ASEAN states and five FTA partners (Australia, China, Japan, NZ, Korea), signed in 2020; India stayed out.

159.s: The first Asian countries summit was held on 14th December, 2005 in :
159.x: The first East Asia Summit was held on 14 December 2005 at Kuala Lumpur with 16 countries including India.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Comprehensive Economic Programme (RCEP).

I. It is an economic cooperation for the China led free trade.

II. It is a counter cooperation for the America led trans-Pacific partnership.

III. In the countries involved in this cooperation Indian Professionals will have job market.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
159.x: RCEP was seen as a counter to the US-led TPP (II) and as opening markets for Indian professionals (III, the key's view); it is ASEAN-led rather than a China-led FTA, so I is rejected.

159.s: South-East Asia has captivated the attention of global community over space and time as a geostrategically significant region. Which among the following is the most convincing explanation for this global perspective?
o: It was the hot theatre during the Second World War.
Its location between the Asian powers of China and India.
Its was the arena of superpower confrontation during the Cold War period.
Its location between the Pacific and Indian oceans and its pre-eminent maritime character.
159.x: Southeast Asia's geostrategic importance rests mainly on its location between the Pacific and Indian Oceans and its maritime character; the other options are historical episodes.

159.s: The 15th ASEAN summit was held in:
159.x: The 15th ASEAN Summit (October 2009) was held at Cha-am / Hua Hin, Thailand.

159.s: Where was the 14 th ASEAN-India Summit organized?
159.x: The 14th ASEAN-India Summit was held on 8 September 2016 in Vientiane, Laos.

159.s: East Timor recently became an independent nation. Before that, under whose rule was East Timor?
159.x:
Most books and keys: Portuguese (colonial ruler till 1975). Strictly: just before independence (2002) East Timor was under Indonesian occupation (1975-99) and UN administration (1999-2002) (general knowledge, not checked).
East Timor was a Portuguese colony until 1975; it was then occupied by Indonesia (1975-99) and run by the UN until independence on 20 May 2002.

159.s: Where was the India ASEAN Inno Tech summit 2019 held?
159.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
159.x: The 2nd ASEAN-India InnoTech Summit (with the Grassroots Innovation Forum) was held at the SMX Convention Center, Davao City, Philippines, on 20-22 November 2019.

159.s: Which of the following is not a member of ASEAN?
159.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
159.x: India is not an ASEAN member (it is a dialogue partner); Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia are members.

159.s: Which is the capital of Vietnam?
159.x: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam; Ho Chi Minh City is its largest city, Beijing and Seoul are other capitals.

159.s: What is the number of member states of ASEAN?
159.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
159.x:
ASEAN had 10 members - now 11, with Timor-Leste admitted in October 2025 (rebuilt notes b2-r159, row 159)
ASEAN had 10 members when this was asked (now 11, after Timor-Leste joined in Oct 2025). 12, 15 and 8 were never right. (Moved to book 2 row 159.)

159.s:
Consider the following statements about ASEAN:
1. It was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 8 August 1967 with five founders.
2. Its Secretariat is at Bangkok.
3. With Timor-Leste (2025), it has 11 members.
4. Myanmar is the only ASEAN country sharing a land border with India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
159.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the ASEAN Secretariat is at Jakarta.

159.s:
Match List-I (India-ASEAN milestone) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Sectoral dialogue partner | i. 1994
b. ASEAN Regional Forum set up | ii. 2022
c. Summit-level partner | iii. 2002
d. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership | iv. 1992
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
159.x: Sectoral dialogue partner 1992; ARF 1994; summit-level partner 2002; Comprehensive Strategic Partnership 2022 (full dialogue partner 1996).

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India-ASEAN relations were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2022.
2. The 21st ASEAN-India Summit (October 2024) was held at Jakarta.
3. The East Asia Summit has 19 members, and its 20th summit at Kuala Lumpur (2025) adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 21st ASEAN-India Summit was at Vientiane, Laos (as was the 14th in 2016).

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP):
1. It was signed on 15 November 2020.
2. It covers about 30% of the world's population.
3. India opted out of it in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India stayed out in November 2019, a year before signing.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mekong Ganga Cooperation:
1. It was launched on 10 November 2000 at Phnom Penh.
2. It has six members, including Cambodia.
3. Its areas include tourism, culture and education, but not defence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the MGC was launched at Vientiane (Laos).

159.s: When was Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) established?
159.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
159.x: APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) was set up in 1989 at Canberra; India is not a member.

159.s: Where was the 14th summit of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) held?
159.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
159.x: The 14th OIC Islamic Summit was held in Mecca (Makkah), Saudi Arabia, on 31 May 2019; the other options are garbled place names.

159.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT true for NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation)?
I. Finland became NATO’s newest member in February 2023.
II. Finland became the 31st country to join NATO.
159.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
159.x: Finland joined NATO on 4 April 2023 as the 31st member, not in February 2023 - so only statement I is not true.

159.s: From the year 2009, NATO will have two new members:
159.x: Croatia and Albania joined NATO in April 2009.

159.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. India is a member of the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) Forum.

II. Russia is a member of North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: India is not an APEC member and Russia is not a NATO member, so neither statement is correct.

159.s: Which one of the following countries is not a member of the Nordic Council?
159.x: The Nordic Council comprises Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden; the United Kingdom is not a member.

159.s: Which country recently joined NATO?
159.x:
Most books and keys: Russia. Strictly: Russia did not join NATO; in May 2002 it joined the NATO-Russia Council as a partner (general knowledge, not checked).
Russia never became a NATO member; the key refers to Russia joining the NATO-Russia Council (Rome, May 2002), while France, Germany and Britain were already members.

159.s: As of January 2020, who was the head of the Commonwealth of Nations?
159.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
159.x:
Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022 — now King Charles III is Head of the Commonwealth (general knowledge, not checked)
In January 2020 the Head of the Commonwealth was Queen Elizabeth II (now King Charles III, since September 2022).

159.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The Commonwealth has no charter, treaty or constitution.

II. All the territories/countries once under the British empire (jurisdiction/ rule/mandate) automatically joined the commonwealth as its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x:
the Commonwealth Charter was adopted in December 2012 and signed on 11 March 2013 — now the Commonwealth has a charter (general knowledge, not checked)
When asked (2010) the Commonwealth had no charter, treaty or constitution (now it has the Commonwealth Charter, 2013); membership is voluntary, so former British territories did not join automatically.

159.s: Which country did not sign the Almaty Charter at the 16-nation summit held in June 2002?

159.x: The Almaty Charter (CICA, June 2002) was signed by India, Kyrgyzstan and Palestine among 16 states; Thailand was not a signatory.

159.s: The latest regional economic bloc to be formed is :

159.s: Asia-Pacific Economic cooperation was founded in

159.s: When was Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) established?
159.src: APPSC AEE Civil & Mechanical Engineering General Studies & M
159.x: APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) was set up in 1989 at Canberra. Off-topic (regional organisations).

159.s: In July 2022, the 30 NATO allies signed off on the accession protocols for which of the following countries?
159.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
159.x: At the NATO summit (Madrid, June 2022) Finland and Sweden were invited; the 30 allies signed their accession protocols on 5 July 2022. Finland joined in April 2023 and Sweden in March 2024.

159.s: Which of the following countries hosted the '2019 NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) Summit'?
159.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
159.x: The NATO leaders' meeting of December 2019 (70th anniversary) was held in London (Watford), the UK.

159.s:
Match List-I (Country) with List-II (Year of joining NATO):
List-I | List-II
a. Croatia and Albania | i. 2024
b. North Macedonia | ii. 2023
c. Finland | iii. 2009
d. Sweden | iv. 2020

159.x: Croatia and Albania 2009; North Macedonia (30th) 27 March 2020; Finland (31st) 4 April 2023; Sweden (32nd) 7 March 2024.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:

3. India is a member of the OECD.

159.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India is not a member of the OECD (Paris).

159.s: Which of the following is not the member of SAARC?

159.x: SAARC's eight members are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka; Myanmar is not a member.

159.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct in respect of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
o: Its Headquarters is located in Kathmandu.
China is the only country with an Observer status in SAARC.
The First SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka.
The First SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka.

159.s: South Asian University is located in which city?
159.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
159.x: South Asian University, a SAARC institution set up in 2010, is in New Delhi.

159.s: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established with the signing of the SAARC Charter in Dhaka in:

159.x: The 31st SAARC Council of Ministers meeting (February 2009) was held in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

159.s: Which one among the following statements about South Asia is not correct?
o: All the countries in South Asia are currently democracies.
SAFTA was signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad.
The US and China play an influential role in the politics of some South Asian states.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about SAARC.

Consider the following pairs:

2. MIKTA — Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye and Australia
3. Quad — India, China, Japan and Australia
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
160.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Quad comprises India, the United States, Japan and Australia, not China; hence pair 3 is false.
160.tq: Use membership composition to catch a swapped-country trap.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Pair 1: **G4** = **India, Brazil, Germany, Japan**; pair 2: **MIKTA** = **Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia**.
Pair 3 wrong: the **Quad** = India, **USA**, Japan, Australia — not China.

The G4 seeks permanent UNSC seats.

xs: The **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** is NOT a Quad initiative — option **(2)**; it is a **BRICS** pool (**2014**, **$100 billion**).
Quad initiatives: **Quad Vaccine Partnership**, **IPMDA**, **Critical and Emerging Technologies** group.

160.s: Consider the following statements about IBSA: 1. It was founded in 2003 through the Brasilia Declaration. 2. The IBSA Trust Fund is managed by the World Bank. 3. IBSAMAR is its naval exercise. Which of the statements given above are correct?

161.x: Statement 1 is wrong: New START was between the USA and Russia (Russia suspended it in 2023). Statement 2 is correct: INF (1987) was a USA-USSR treaty and the US withdrew in 2019. So 2 only (B); A, C and D misjudge one of the two.

xs: Only statement 2 is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.
Statement 1: **New START (2010)** was between the **USA and Russia**, not China — wrong.
Statement 2: The **INF Treaty (1987)** was **USA-USSR**, and the **US withdrew in 2019** — correct.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT).

I. The Treaty cames into force only if and when all nuclear countries sign it.

II. Iraq and India have not signed the treaty.
Which of the following statements given above is/are correct?
161.x:
Some keys give 'Only II' (Iraq and India have not signed); that was true only before August 2008.
Neither statement is correct: the CTBT enters into force only when all 44 Annex-2 States ratify it (signature by 'all nuclear countries' is not the condition), and Iraq signed the CTBT on 19 August 2008 – only India of the two had not signed.

161.s:

1. China
2. France
3. India
4. Israel
5. Pakistan Which among the above are Nuclear Weapons States as recognised by the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, commonly known as the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
161.x: Only China and France of the options are NPT Nuclear Weapon States (tested before 1 January 1967); India, Israel and Pakistan are outside the NPT.

161.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
161.x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.
161.tq: Separate India's objection to the treaty from the treaty's stated prohibition.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound disarmament** and still **allows subcritical tests** — option **(1)**.
The CTBT (**1996**) **bans all nuclear explosions**, so option (3) is wrong; it is a nuclear, not chemical, treaty.
It says nothing about recognising nuclear-weapon states — that is the **NPT**, which recognises the **P5**.
xa: The CTBT is **not in force**.
The **PTBT (1963)** bans tests **except underground**; **India is a party** to it.
India **did not sign the TPNW** (in force **2021**) — it "adds nothing to customary law".
⚠ India is not a party to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

2. Its Review Conferences are held every ten years.
3. It recognises as Nuclear Weapon States those that tested a nuclear device before 1 January 1967.

161.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: NPT Review Conferences are held every five years.

161.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: MTCR – 1987 – Missiles and drones (500 kg over 300 km)

The **Australia Group** (**1985**) covers **chemical and biological weapon precursors**.
The **Hague Code of Conduct** (**2002**) deals with **ballistic missile proliferation** (transparency).

161.x: The Hague Code of Conduct concerns ballistic-missile transparency; Wassenaar covers conventional arms and the Australia Group chemical and biological precursors.

161.x: The Australia Group was formed in 1985; India became its 43rd member in 2018.

161.s: What does the India-specific NSG waiver of 2008, associated with the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal, permit India to do?

join the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state

161.tq: Distinguish the practical effect of a waiver from formal membership in another treaty.
xs: The **2008 NSG waiver** lets India carry out **civil nuclear trade** and **import uranium and reactors** — option **(1)**.
It came through the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal**; it does not make India an NPT member or give it a veto.
The NSG is **consensus-based**, so no member holds a special veto through the waiver.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; Additional Protocol = **2014**.
Uranium deals followed: **Canada (10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035)** and **Australia (July 2026)**.
The **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement** covers civilian facilities and **excludes military** ones.

161.s: What mainly blocks India's entry into the Nuclear Suppliers Group?

164.s:
With reference to Home Guards, consider the following statements:
1. Home Guards are raised under the Home Guards Act and Rules of the Central Government.
2. The role of the Home Guards is to serve as an auxiliary force to the police in maintenance of internal security.
3. To prevent infiltration on the international border/coastal areas, the Border Wing Home Guards Battalions have been raised in some States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
164.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct – Home Guards are an auxiliary to the police for internal security, and Border Wing Home Guards battalions exist in border States. Statement 1 is wrong: they are raised under the Home Guards Acts and Rules of the States/UTs, not a central Act.

164.s: Border Security Force (BSF) is responsible for guarding on borders of which countries?
164.x: The BSF guards India's borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh; Nepal and Bhutan are SSB, China is ITBP.

164.x: The BSF was raised on 1 December 1965, after the 1965 war.

o: a branch of the Indian Navy.
an organisation under the Central Board of Excise and Customs.
an organisation under the Ministry of Defence.
a para-military force under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

164.s:
Which of the following is/are Paramilitary force(s) of India?

I. Indian Coast Guard

II. Assam Rifles

III. Directorate General of Resettlement
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

164.x: BSF was raised in 1965, ITBP in 1962, SSB in 1963 and the Coast Guard in 1978.

164.s: The ITBP guards the high-altitude China border from the Karakoram Pass to which place?
164.x: The ITBP, raised in 1962, guards the China border from Karakoram Pass to Jachep La, with posts at 9,000–18,800 feet.

164.x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border. The BSF, ITBP and SSB are correctly matched with their principal border responsibilities.

xs: **Assam Rifles — Bangladesh border** is wrong: **Assam Rifles** guards the **Myanmar** border — option **(1)**.
The **Bangladesh** border is guarded by the **BSF** (with Pakistan).
**SSB – Nepal and Bhutan**, **ITBP – China**, **BSF – Pakistan and Bangladesh** are correct.
xa: ⚠ Oldest = **Assam Rifles** (**1835**); **SSB** = **newest border force**.
**BSF** (**1965**) has **193 battalions** (incl. **3 NDRF**).

164.s: The Coast Guard is responsible for coastal security in territorial waters and functions under which Ministry?

Coastline: **11,098.81 km**.

164.x: BSF jurisdiction in Punjab and West Bengal was extended from 15 km to 50 km; States objected as Police and Public Order are in the State List.

**VVP-II** (**2024-25 to 2028-29**) develops border villages.

164.x: The CRPF began on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.

164.x: Assam Rifles was raised in 1835; the BSF dates from 1965, the ITBP from 1962 and the SSB from 1963.

164.x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border, not Bangladesh, which is with the BSF.

164.x: The ITBP was raised in 1962 after the Chinese aggression; it guards the 3,488 km China border.

164.x: The Coast Guard was set up in 1977; it guards territorial waters under the Ministry of Defence.

164.x: The SSB was raised in 1963 as the Special Service Bureau; it now guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders.

164.x: Phase I covers China-border states; VVP-II covers the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.
